So, after thinking of ways I could make more of an input on here until I start undergoing journals - I have decided to leave detailed strain reviews. Reviews based on what I smell, see, taste, feel and ultimately the bud as a whole. I mean I go through alot and I get new flavours every time. So why not?

 

 #1 Blueberry Cheesecake 

Blueberry x White Cheese

Indica

18% THC

For starters, before the package got within 2 meters of me - the old school aroma of sweet, cheesy berries just overwhelmed me. I found my mind instantly taken to the good old days, and oh boy it just gets sweeter and sweeter the closer you get. This really is up there for aromas. Not much will compete with a real stinky, potent cheese, and the fruity aftertaste that the blueberry adds really is a compliment.

I've smoked this a few times in the past - quality ranging from 2/10 to 10/10. I'd put what I have at a solid 6/10. It's bark is definitely worse than its bite. Smells amazing. Looks and breaks apart incredibly with an array of crystals and white clouds between every tear. Beautifully presented with a stunning lime green canvas, smothered in bright orange ivy. I'd really like it to smoke her as she smells but this time around she just lacks that punch. You know your smoking Blue Cheese but almost feel cheated by the climax. She gets the endorphins going for sure, she leaves a stunning first impression when you get your hands on her and indulge in the sugary scent - but she's definitely a mellow and mild smoke. A good wake and bake and a great smoke for those who have their daily responsibilities and still need to get shit done.....

6/10

Wake and bake 

Average

Be safe

items.name_norm: 2021 indoor soil bruce banner 3 senorita bruce grow journal
items.thread_title: 2021 Indoor, Soil, Bruce Banner #3, Senorita Bruce, Grow Journal
items.grow_notes:
Hey Everyone,

While a long time partier, I am brand new to the board here and a first time grower as well so could really use everyone's experience as I find my way through my first grow. I am not an overly talkative guy but I need to opine a little on my setup so you can help me better.

Basics:

 
 Indoor Grow 
 I wanted to grow a Girl Scout Cookie Gelato cross but it didn't germ so as Thanos would have it, I am growing a Bruce Banner #3, from Sensible Seeds. 
 BB#3 is a feminized, sativa dominant hybrid, ~65day flower cycle, susceptible to early CA/MG deficiency, fussy about temp and RH to get max potency/yield (so I read), and stinky 
 Equipment: Spyderfarm 2'3"x2'3"x5' tent with 170CFM/m exhaust fan and carbon filter and SF1000W LED w/dimmer (note: the carbon filter is mounted inside the tent and the inline fan outside the tent due to space constraints) 
 Environment: As a new grower this is where I am spending my time, trying to learn the tent, exhaust and oscillating fans, and humidifier to control temperature and RH. Averages over past 3 days: Temp/RH: 78.5/65.2%, 77.6/67.7%, 76.8/66.6 
 Soil Mix: 3 parts Fox Farm Happy Frog to 1 part washed, coarse Perlite + .5 TBLSP fine
items.excerpt:
Hey Everyone,

While a long time partier, I am brand new to the board here and a first time grower as well so could really use everyone's experience as I find my way through my first grow. I am not an overly talkative guy but I need to opine a little on my setup so you can help me better.

Basics:

 
 Indoor Grow 
 I wanted to grow a Girl Scout Cookie Gelato cross but it didn't germ so as Thanos would have it, I am growing a Bruce Banner #3, from Sensible Seeds. 
 BB#3 is a feminized, sativa dominant hybrid, ~65day flower cycle, susceptible to early CA/MG deficiency, fussy about temp and RH to get max potency/yield (so I read), and stinky 
 Equipment: Spyderfarm 2'3"x2'3"x5' tent with 170CFM/m exhaust fan and carbon filter and SF1000W LED w/dimmer (note: the carbon filter is mounted inside the tent and the inline fan outside the tent due to space constraints) 
 Environment: As a new grower this is where I am spending my time, trying to learn the tent, exhaust and oscillating fans, and humidifier to control temperature and RH. Averages over past 3 days: Temp/RH: 78.5/65.2%, 77.6/67.7%, 76.8/66.6 
 Soil Mix: 3 parts Fox Farm Happy Frog to 1 part washed, coarse Perlite + .5 TBLSP fine dolomite lime. This will mix up to scale 
 Containers: Peat Cube to 4" peat pot to 1 gallon fabric pot to 5 gallon fabric pot 
 Fertilizers: FoxFarm, Fertiloam Root Stimulator 
 Grow Update 1 : Senorita Bruce is 2 weeks old today and while she is a little stretchy, I think she looks good (picts to follow) but would love everyone's thoughts. As history, I germinated the seeds in water for 24 hours then moved them to a Jiffy Peat Cube and dome/darkness/warmth until the first sign of growth, then moved the dome into the tent, turned on lights at 18-6, and hardened out of the dome over week 1. In week 2, this past week, I transplanted the peat cube into a 4" peat pot using the soil mix noted above and give her Fertiloam Root Stimulator every other water (twice now) from "the bottom up". She is about 7-8" from light with the light at about 60-70% intensity and seems to be enjoying herself.

I have one major concern, odor. Simply put, one whiff of this in the house and she will need to come down. I have her in a discrete place, she won't be found unless she gives herself away, and I don't anticipate problems during veg. However, during the later days of flowering, I am nervous that the carbon filter wont be good enough, especially with this strain. I thought about buying a second in-line fan and carbon scrubber and running it in the room, outside the tent, if the smell cant be contained with the single system. 

Please comfort me with tales of how you have seen this work before....

items.grow_notes:
Welcome to another outdoor grow attempt in this vast space of wildlife and critters! It's always a battle, and I never know what surprises lie in store from daylight to dark.

First a few photos of the set up out there. It's an old planter area that had wood posts surrounding it, and they have degraded and rotted over the years. I've cleaned out the brush and most of the grasses, and left the Trumpet Vine plants there. I have cages around the plants, and solo cups with the bottoms cut off inserted about 2" into the soil around the seedlings to help protect from certain critters. So far, it's working out pretty good.

The temperatures have been way too cool for June, so they are in limbo waiting for a reason to get growing. Today is a warm up beginning, finally. Nights will be high fifties F. to low sixties.

First a video, the outdoor area is shortly after the indoor grow, then some photos:

items.name: 3x300W LED, Purple Kush, Scrog, Soil, Grow
items.name_norm: 3x300w led purple kush scrog soil grow
items.thread_title: 3x300W LED, Purple Kush, Scrog, Soil, Grow
items.grow_notes:
After an original starter grow that lasted from April through Sept with numerous ups and downs (the web is full of useful and NOT so useful information) I yielded around 2-5oz (it's still curing) so I'm happy. what next? Well this grow of course 



I'm hoping with posting along the way with this grow that I not only gain useful information from the community but I also give something to it as well. 



So to start, here is the base.



Lighting consists of 

1 - Apollo 300w (100x3w LEDs) 

2 - Apollo 300w (60x5w LEDs) 

My original plan was to go with 2 of the 100x3w but since the model was discontinued for the 5w, I opted for 2 of the newer model (along with the original) for total coverage. I added the 2 new towards the end of the flower on my last so I am excited to see how having all three from the start will go. I opted for LED's for a few reasons.. but mostly because I'm a geek and enjoy anything LED 

 

All will be in an Apollo 48"x24"x60" tent which was perfect for my original 3. I keep the apartment smelling (or not rather) with an iPower 4-Inch Inline Carbon Air Filter. I also circulate the inner air with a 10" oscillating fan

Now I am looking at regular strains in order of potential high THC, low CBD contribution without in-breeding.

1/ Hardcore OG Regular.

2/ Runtz Regular. 

3/ Gorilla Glue #4 Regular.

 

4/ Blackberry Moonrocks Regular.

5/ Fatkid’s Cake Regular. 

6/ Bruce Banner Regular.

items.excerpt:
Amnesia Flash Strain review

Anesia Amnesia Flash from the best Dutch strains, which were chosen for their strength and intense. Amnesia Flash is perfectly suitable both, for outdoors as well as for indoors. It has a strong growth and is very resistant against mildew and parasites, therefore it is well suited for beginners and experienced growers as well. Amnesia Flash needs 65 days flowering time in the grow room – outdoor, it can be harvested in mid-October. She throws off monstrous yields of 700 grams per square meter and more than 1000 g per plant in sunny areas.

Amnesia Flash has a very intense floral aroma and a spicy flavor. The effects are very relaxing for the body and mind activating for the head. The hit of Amnesia Flash is anything but gentle, coming on fast and strong, taking over your mind and body for several hours.

The buds of Amnesia Flash are very large, conic and covered with resin. She is an impressive yielder, and her potency will make the most hardened of smokers go weak at the knees. She will impress experienced and commercial growers and produces an absolute premium weed by giving her the right conditions.

Growing Amnesia Flash

This strain grows to a medium height with short internodal distances. The plants have a bushy structure and a high resistance to mold. Give her an extra week for flowering to increase the extreme resin production.

Medical Use

Amnesia is great for killing your lethargy and helps you stay energetic. In addition to that, it is good for treating depression, anxiety and stress. Therefore, patients of these conditions can use it without any worry. It can also be used for relieving nausea and migraine.

Effects

Creative, Energizing, Euphoria, Happy, Uplifting

May Relieve

Anxiety, Arthritis, Bipolar Disorder, Chronic Pain, Depression, Eye Pressure, Headaches, Mood Swings, Muscle Spasms, PTSD, Stress, Tremors

Flavors - Citrus, Pine, Sweet

Aromas - Citrus, Diesel, Earthy, Pungent, Sour

Yield: 700g/m2; 1000 g/plant

Genetics: 80% Indica / 20% Sativa

Flowering time: 65 days

Outdoor harvest: mid of October

Suitable for indoors and outdoors

Height: 100-140 cm • 150-200 cm

THC: 27%

Conclusion.

If you haven’t had to grow this strain don’t wait any longer. I would place this strain as a must grow .

She grows fast and demands her own space; so, she can spread her bud heavy branches where every she wants. When I say she is bud heavy she will need support in order for the branches not to break. They get there fast in flower.

As for growing, she was a breeze, requiring not special treatment.

items.grow_notes:
keep in mind I DO NOT grow autoflowers properly. I grow them as a bumper crop and throw a couple in my veg area for s & g. They get the same feed as my photoperiods wether they like it or not. they get no light adjustment. They just exist in the veg area. For their last couple weeks I do keep the humidity in the 50's. temps are usually in mid 70's.

So knowing that, Apple Fritter auto has the largest buds I have ever grown "improperly"on an auto and the nose is quite delicious. It has been 81 days since the seed has popped and I suspect it has 10 - 14 days or more left. Got to say, I am quite impressed and gonna have to order some more as this was a freebie that I got with a purchase.

BBB

Blueberry x Thin Mint Girl Scout Cookies x Sunset Sherbert

23% THC

Type of buzz - Quite a light hearted ride. I've been smoking this in the morning simply because of its wake and bake qualities. Munchies. Giggles are pretty rife. Energising.

Best uses - Wake and bake. Perfect for a regular smoker who wants to keep it light during the day. Before food. During a gathering, this gets your imagination going and ready for those random conversation

Auto Monkey Seeds- Cherry Pie Auto

This strain grows extremely easily and vigorously. It doesn’t really require training, as the side branching develops very well on its own. It can handle high PPFD levels without issues and is quite a heavy feeder when it comes to nutrients.

For me, the most important factor in evaluating a strain is how it makes me feel — and this one definitely delivers in that regard.

Despite having very dense and heavy buds, I didn’t experience any mold issues during a relatively long 16-day drying period.

Interestingly, even though one of my other autoflowers had a spider mite problem, they didn’t seem interested in this plant — or maybe the other one was just more appealing to them.

CO₂: No direct supplementation (had a mushroom CO₂ bag in the room, but it was likely no longer effective)

Environment: Focused on maintaining proper VPD by constantly adjusting humidity according to temperature

Total Grow Time: 12 weeks

Total Harvest: 300g

Effects

Environment: Focused on maintaining proper VPD by constantly adjusting humidity according to temperature

Total Grow Time: 12 weeks

Total Harvest: 300g

Effects

The initial effect brings a nice sense of relaxation. It doesn’t completely lock you to the couch, but it doesn’t make you overly energetic either. It’s great for watching movies or shows. If you consume a bit more, you can start to notice some sativa-like effects.

I didn’t experience any increase in appetite.

I’d estimate the THC level to be around 18–20%.

The terpene density is quite high.

Toward the end of the cycle, the plant naturally tends to fade quite a bit. Even without flushing , you can achieve clean-burning buds with white ash.

items.excerpt:
Banana Pudding – Herbies Seeds strain review.

Banana Pudding is a flavorful hybrid bred from the infamous Girl Scout Cookies and Banana OG strains, Indica-dominant (70/30), and perfect for banana-lovers. It was originally grown by Dying Breed Seeds out of Mendocino in California. The flavor is sweet, creamy, tinged with vanilla, nuts, and fruit, and has a scent to match. The high is a result of a brain-breaking THC average that can exceeds 30% and comes with a myriad of physical and mental effects. Most people who try the strain are at a loss for words.

Banana Pudding is an indica dominant hybrid strain (70% indica/30% sativa) created through crossing the delicious Girl Scout Cookies X Banana OG strains. Named for its delicious flavor, Banana Pudding is the perfect bud for any indica lover who's after a great taste with their medicine, too.

Like its name suggests, Banana Pudding packs a sweet and creamy sugary banana flavor with hints of fresh vanilla and touches of nuttiness. The aroma is very similar, with a sweet and creamy overtone that's accented by lightly spicy nuttiness and fresh bananas. The Banana Pudding high is just as delicious, with super relaxing physical effects that will soon have you feeling rested.

It starts with a lifting sense that fills the brain with a giggly and unfocused energy. You'll find your mind rushing through happy thoughts while you easily carry on conversations with those around you. As you chat on and on, your body will begin to drop off into a super relaxed state that soon turns heavy and sedative, leaving you hopelessly couch-locked before you know it.

Combined with its super high 30-31% average THC level and 0-1% CBD level, these effects make Banana Pudding a great choice for treating conditions such as depression, headaches or migraines, nausea or appetite loss, chronic pain and chronic stress. This bud has small grape-shaped minty green nugs with lots of thin orange hairs and a coating of tiny frosty white crystal trichomes.

Its major terpenes include Limonene, Caryophyllene, and Linalool, which conspire together on Banana Pudding’s flavor. The result is a lot like its namesake, with tones of sweet sugar, vanilla, cream, and bananas. However, the other terpenes, Caryophyllene in particular, really start to come out on the exhale with a flavor of spicy earth, herbs, and nuts. The main thing to realize is that Banana Pudding is delicious – it’s built its entire reputation on being so.

Its effects are more far-reaching than just the Zen satisfaction of tasting something creamy-delicious (and packed with bananas). The strain provides a feeling of mental ease and calm, which stimulates your brain for creative tasks, so long as they’re relaxing enough. Users report ideal pastimes on Banana Pudding as being things like knitting, drawing, painting, doing puzzles, improving their yoga routines, getting intimate with their lovers, hanging out with friends, and even catching up on some sleep.

With banana on your breath (and calmness in your heart), the effects of this strain can help you work through your depression or a bad migraine. Since the strain increases appetite, you may be able to regulate your eating schedule on Banana Pudding, especially if stress is one of the things that prevents you from eating.

As with any cannabis, dosage is important and effects will vary, but many use Banana Pudding’s ridiculously high — high to give themselves an empowering boost of ease and creative ambition. This doesn’t mean the strain is for everyone, but experienced users (and banana fans) should definitely look it up.

Hope this helps.

Be safe, and grow well my friends,

Tok..

items.grow_notes:
I'm a bit late to the party, but I should be getting my seeds in the next couple of days. 

My plan is to grow one plant outdoors and one plant indoors. For the outdoor plant, I'll put it in a 20 gallon fiber pot using Fox Farms Ocean Forest soil. I think I'll use my standard outdoor nutrient regimen which consists of the Emerald Harvest line of nutrients with some Terpinator. I hope to keep the plant's height down to no more than 5 feet tall. My reasoning is that I'm going after quality over quantity. I could get close to 2 lbs if I let the thing grow to 7 feet tall, but I don't need that much weed. I feel that by keeping it smaller, the plant can concentrate it's energy on less buds sites -- much like grape growers do for the wine industry. Lights: @ViparSpectra PS2000 x 2 daisy chained and 1 Viparspectra XS1500pro

Nutrients: @green leaf Nutrients MegaCrop plus Epsom, Ammonium Sulfate, Potassium Chloride, and Potassium Silicate

items.thread_title: Barney's Farm - Pink Kush In Coco
items.grow_notes:
Hi Folks, Here is some basic information about this grow.

Lights, I start with single 54w cob for seedling then add second cob for 104w then add 300w bar light and remove both cobs then add both cobs again later in flower for total of 408w.

Canna coco brick, I will never buy ready to go coco bagged again they always had gnats.

Nutrients, I use Flairform the complete range except sometimes i don't use the Budgenie..i follow the recommend dose chart.

16/8 hrs light for seedling to veg.

12/12 flower

The winter period has started and i have added 2 x 120w heat tubes that is connected to a digital thermostat..It's good for the cold nights and during the day.

Currently feeding twice a day.

i haven't smoked any weed in 4 months i hope this finishes good.

Seedling complete transplanted into 2 gallon bag.

items.excerpt:
Hi all, 

Budlovski here with a strain and smoke review for my recently dried Bloody skunk Auto by sweet seeds .





 Strain Name - Bloody Skunk



 From - Sweet seeds 



 When - harvested 27/3/15 



 Price - not sure, bought a 3 pack of seeds online.



 Type - Ruderalis indica/sativa, started off with slower indica growth after a couple of nodes took off and stretched with sativa/ruderalis growth.



 Appearance - Bloody Skunk produced quite dense nuggets all around especially in the top main cola, the buds were a medium purple coloured with green fan leaves and half purple and green bud leaves. The dried bud went very dark purple almost black making the orange hairs seem neon and bright, had beautiful trichome colouring around leaf edges and deep inside.



 Smell - She had many mixed smells this girl, during growth she went through nearly every smell you could think of, once harvested her buds smell softened a little, however still pungent, very skinny and seemed to have strong hints of coofee aswell as a sweeter fruity undertone, overall its a very smooth beautiful smell.



 Taste - had a great taste yet not extremely powerful, when inhaling its very smooth almost a creamy coffee taste inhaling then exhaling you got abit more of the slinky weed flavours hanging around on the tongue. Its an extremely smooth smoke in fact probably the smoothest I've had but it gives you that tiny tickle in the throat to let you know you smoked it 



 Type of Buzz - I believe it was a very pleasant high, and that means something coming from me since I stopped smoking due to anxiety problems, so now I only taste test what I grow and a lower tolerance really helps to know the high in a way. Anyways it was very relaxing, had a joint after watching the blood moon eclipse and I was sitting outside fully relaxed I was relatively stress free, the anxiety I usually get smoking very minor. Its just a very nice mix of A body stone and a cerebral high however definately more on the relaxation side.



 Length of Buzz - 1-1 1/2 hours then I drifted off to sleep peacefully too.



 Best Medicinal Use - From what I could tell and feel, Bloody Skunk would be well suited for people with problems like insomnia, stress, comfort, appetite and is say pain since it gave the body a weightless seperate feeling.



 Overall - Too sum up this strain I've got to say for nice colourful good quality Autoflowers this ones on my Auto list whenever I grow them. Took 10 weeks from seed to harvest so depending on the high you want you could intact harvest anywhere between 8 or 9 weeks to 11 or 12 weeks. An absolute delight to grow just make sure you keep the nutes on a low level to begin with. Doesn't take up much space reached just over 47cm high with one main cola and a very little low side branches. I've read there can be a bit of A pheno varient so if choosing this strain you'd probably be safer to get a 3 pack or something just too make sure you can get a beautiful purple one.

I have another 2 bloody skunk seeds and 1 of the mother red poison so I can't wait for the day I can use a longer light schedule again and grow them out.

I havnt mention but this strain goes purple regardless of temperature, unlike a lot that need to be grown in a cooler temperature.

items.grow_notes:
Hi friends, I’m gonna do my best to create a decent journal here and I invite and encourage your feedback - because I’m a NOOB and the all caps wasn’t an accident.

My journey begins with a MOP (Mimosa Orange Punch) seedling from my friend and former FD colleague Brian from the WOW Factory.

Strain: Mimosa Orange Punch

Genetic Makeup: Indica dominant hybrid

Pot Size: 10 gallon

Environment: Outdoor

Stage: Pre Flower / Early Bloom

Medium: WOW Factory provided soil

Nutrients: Miracle Gro x 1 weekly

Pests: Leafhoppers

Watering: as needed per my Noob level analog soil meter, but an average of 4x’s a week.

Pics are from where we started back in May and where we are now. As well as a couple pests (leafhopper and larvae)?

So far all I’ve done is try to find the sweet spot for watering (told ya I was a huge NOOB) and applied Dr Killigans Doom and Bloom spray for the leafhoppers.

Every Sunday this lovely lady gets Miracle Gro.

Two weeks ago I repotted from a 10 gal bag to a 20, using Fox Farms Ocean Forest as backfill.

Thanks for sharing your experiences and happy growing everyone!

items.grow_notes:
Hey Rocketers! 

This thing is a total beast, man. It's a balanced hybrid that hits you with a powerful punch. I'm talking a whopping 27% THC, so you know it's gonna knock you on your ass. But the best part is, it's not just a one-dimensional high. It's got a nice cerebral buzz that'll elevate your mood, followed by a relaxing body stone that's perfect for unwinding after a long day.

Now, growing this new strain isn't a walk in the park. It's a bit finicky and needs precise conditions. You gotta keep a close eye on humidity and watch out for pests and mold. But if you can give it the attention it deserves, the rewards are huge.

 Here's what I've learned from growing Bio Jesus : 

 
 Start with quality seeds: Get your seeds from a reputable source to ensure a healthy and vigorous plant. Rocketseeds.com 
 Germination: I prefer the paper towel method for germination. It's simple and effective. 
 Vegetative stage: Give your plants plenty of light and nutrients during this stage. I usually keep them in a vegetative state for 3-4 weeks. 
 Flowering stage: This is where the magic happens. Reduce the light cycle to 12/12 to induce flowering. Be prepared for some serious bud production!

Considering all the hype about these brands, I had to give it a go. So as it says, we got cheetah piss, from the cookies brand. First impression.....nice little nugs. A decent gassy woft from opening the little bag quickly dissapates to just regular old weed smells. As I said, the nugs are nice. Small....but very dense. Kinda felt like handling crack rocks. Lol....not that I've done that, but thats what they reminded me of. Taste is EH.....not much there. High is also mediocre. Not very dimensional. Kind of generic IMO. Lol overall it's some decent bud, but definitely not worth the hype. 

Looks: 6/10

Smell: 3/10

Flavor:3/10

High: 5/10

items.name: Christmas Buds! Mid 1990's strain: Anyone remember and know what strain?
items.name_norm: christmas buds mid 1990 s strain anyone remember and know what strain
items.thread_title: Christmas Buds! Mid 1990's strain: Anyone remember and know what strain?
items.grow_notes:
Hey everyone....



Back in Chicagoland and I believe throughout the midwest, around every Christmas there used to be a strain that came out called Christmas buds. I mentioned this on another thread but felt it deserved its own thread in search of what it exactly was. 



These buds were so delicious, a mix between a pinetree and a peppermint candy cane and were nice pinecone shaped buds, very dense, with bright green and bright red hairs. I remember just a small 1 hitter packed with the christmas nugs was very strong and would hit your lungs like you just inhaled quick dry cement...very very strong high....



I have been wondering for years if anyone knows what strain or genetics these "christmas buds" came from? I know that I have seen people saying, "its just some bud that someone put a name on" which I highly doubt is true because it was consistant for a few years in a row that I could remember, always the same taste, look, and heavy inhale...



I would love to hear if anyone knows anything about this strain/cut/genetics because I would love to see if their still available and get my hands on some Also would love to see how many people got a chance to experience this

items.name_norm: citrus slurp from original sensible seeds
items.thread_title: Citrus Slurp From Original Sensible Seeds
items.grow_notes:
Hello everyone!

 @Original Sensible Seeds were kind enough to send me some seeds of one of their newer strains called Citrus Slurp! 

It's a balanced (50/50) hybrid, bred from Orange Cookies x Watermelon.

I'm a sucker for citrus flavours, and balanced hybrids, so this one should be right up my alley!

It reportedly grows well in cool, hot, and temperate climates, with a flowering period of 55-65 days, so it should enjoy the summer outdoors here in Southern Ontario.

The flavour and scent are described as sweet and zesty, reminiscent of oranges, grapefruit, and candied watermelon. The dominant terpenes are myrcene, limonene, and terpinolene.

The effects are described as clear and uplifting, with mental clarity without overstimulation, and relaxation without couch lock.

I'll be growing her in a 60 litre fabric pot of rich soil, with Mega Crop from @Greenleaf Nutrients as needed.

I put in a seed to soak yesterday, and today she has a tail peeking out, so she has been planted in a 750ml pot.

 Citrus Slurp 

 @Original Sensible Seeds

items.thread_title: CMan420: Mimosa x Orange Punch Comparative Grow, Barney's Farm, in a SIP
items.grow_notes:
Welcome to my comparative grow!

I am probably a mid-skilled grower with a number of years under my belt, but always still learning something new about growing this plant. I use a combination of Quad-Lining & Defoliation techniques to maximize growth/bud potential and Quad-Lining produces a nice flat canopy so its all top-buds. I also use compost + soil in a custom made SIP bucket . SIPs are the laziest way to grow I've found, and can produce hydro-like results if all goes well.

I'm very excited to try out this strain, just need my seeds!

Strain: Mimosa x Orange Punch from @Barneys Farm 

Genetic Makeup: Hybrid 

Pot or Bucket Size: 5 Gall SIP 

Tent Size: 4x4 

Grow Space : 2x2Veg 4x4Flower 

How Many Plants: 1 

Environment: Indoor 

Stage: Starting from seed 

Medium: Soil + Compost 

Lights: Vipar LED Panels: XS1500 & XS2500 

Nutrients: MegaCrop line 

Temperature: Averages around 20 degrees Celcius, warmer towards summer 

Relative Humidity: Averages just over 30 percent humidity 

Pests: Just me 

Watering Schedule: I let the SIP go through its phases of wet to dry then top up

 Appearance - Vigorous branching shrub to 6-8' tall

 Smell - Skunk, Woody, Spicy

 Taste - Smooth, easy to smoke

 Type of Buzz - Perfect blend of intense head high and body high

 Length of Buzz - 3-4 hours

 Best Medicinal Use - appetite enhancement, pain relief, anti-anxiety

I'm a brain cancer survivor, disease free since Jan. 2022. Cannabis was a godsend in battling side effects of chemo. Been growing my own herb for three years now. Lebanese landrace has been a favorite, likely due to high levels of CBD and CBG. I've been making crosses and this is a winner.

Female: Original Haze. This is a three way cross of Columbian sativas, used as foundation for Haze strain. Sourced from Authentic Genetics. Tall and wildly sprawling plants, not suitable for outdoor grow as I live at 45 degrees N latitude. Great strain, reminds me of the Columbian Gold I smoked 50 years ago.

Male: Lebanese landrace, sourced from justcannabisseeds.com. Famous for the legendary Lebanese hash, this is an ideal strain for my hot and dry high desert climate. Love this strain. Very smooth and tasty smoke. Relaxing and mildly euphoric clear headed high. No means of testing, but it has high levels of CBD and CBG.

From this cross, I got seven seeds. Five made it past seedling stage. They grew outdoors directly in the ground. All five of those plants were FEMALE. No males sad to say. Plants showed great hybrid vigor. Narrow leaves and bushy growth. Harvested in first week of October, a win for me. Trichomes fully cloudy at harvest.

Brought cuttings into the grow room under LED for breeding, see photos below. Applied silver thiosulphate to select buds to initiate growth of pollen sacs for breeding. The STS reversal worked, but too late as my females outdoors were late in flower, not receptive to pollen. So no seed increase, but I did use pollen from Brazil Amazonia to create seeds. That might be a very special cross, will know more when I plant next Spring. 

This is obviously an unique strain which cannot be found in any dispensary. Have been growing other landraces with great results. The Middle Eastern hash plants in particular thrive in my climate.

items.name: Corn seed sprout tea
items.name_norm: corn seed sprout tea
items.thread_title: Corn seed sprout tea
items.grow_notes:
I am going to try a corn seed sprouted tea. 

I believe they should be used when tap root first shows, as opposed to sprouts for eating.

I soaked 1/4 cup for 12 hours in tap well water pH 8.3. 

Rinse 2x daily for 24 hours.

Should be ready tonight.

Now this is ultra low cost and not organic.

I bought a 50 lb bag at tractor supply for <$20. This is intended for livestock supplemental feeds. 

My intention was to feed local squirrels to hopefully keep them away from bird feeders.

I have been experimenting with sprouts for personal consumption and figured I would try to make this.

I know there pesticides, were likely used, but they have been washed and my plants are still in veg. I eat non organic meats so I dont think it would be any worse from a health stand point. Not sure how my microbes in the soil will like it.

After I put early sprouts in a blender I was going to seperate the solids and dilute the liquid with a gallon of spring water pH 'd to 6.5 or so and give with next watering,

I probably will make a ferment from the solids (with a KNF method using equal part sugar) and use to feed later.

I'll update and see how plants respond.

I soaked 1/4 cup for 12 hours in tap well water pH 8.3. 

Rinse 2x daily for 24 hours.

Should be ready tonight.

Now this is ultra low cost and not organic.

I bought a 50 lb bag at tractor supply for <$20. This is intended for livestock supplemental feeds. 

My intention was to feed local squirrels to hopefully keep them away from bird feeders.

I have been experimenting with sprouts for personal consumption and figured I would try to make this.

I know there pesticides, were likely used, but they have been washed and my plants are still in veg. I eat non organic meats so I dont think it would be any worse from a health stand point. Not sure how my microbes in the soil will like it.

After I put early sprouts in a blender I was going to seperate the solids and dilute the liquid with a gallon of spring water pH 'd to 6.5 or so and give with next watering,

I probably will make a ferment from the solids (with a KNF method using equal part sugar) and use to feed later.

I'll update and see how plants respond.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 Welcome One & All!​ 

The main focus of this journal is to provide new growers with information about some of the basic requirements needed to grow cannabis successfully. Additionally I am looking to increase my own skill set and knowledge about this awesome plant. Also it’s just to have a bit of fun.

I have grown cannabis for quite a few years, but I don’t want to come off as a “ know it all ” or give the impression that I am a very experienced grower. I am not that! I have grown somewhere around 10-15 cycles, so take that into account when you consider taking any advice from me!

I did not plan to make this journal, so I already started the seeds a while ago. I’m not gonna cheap out on this journal though, so here is what I have done so far.

 Background ​ 

I started these seeds on the 24th of January.

The method I used for germination is the following:

 
 I soak the seeds in plain tap water for 12-24 hours. 
 I fill up my 2L/0.5gal pots with soil and add 0.2L of plain tap water before sowing. 
 I sow the seeds in the pots and cover the pots with plastic. 
 I wait till I see the young sprouts break through the soil. When this happens I will remove the plastic. 
 That’s it!

I find this method to be fool-proof. I used to do the paper towel method, with and without a plastic bag and that method works too. But with this method there is zero chance that you damage the tap-root when sowing it because the seed most likely didn’t grow much of a tap root before sowing.

Covering the pot with plastic will make sure that the seed will stay moist. If the newly activated seed dry out, it will die! So at this stage it is crucial to keep the seed moist. For new growers, it is very common to over nurture your plants. Some say that new growers tend to kill their plants with love and I would agree with that. You are going on a new adventure, learning things and you are passionate about your plants, so naturally you want to create the best conditions for them to thrive in. Unfortunately new growers don’t have the experience required to determine what the best conditions are; So the plants may get too much water or too many nutrients in the solution; When all the plant really needs is be left alone, so it can be allowed to do its own thing.

items.grow_notes:
This is a delayed smoke report. I wanted to wait until everything had time to cure (or nearly cured.) And then after that happened and I started smoking it, I forgot for a few weeks about doing the report. 

This is the smoke and tell from my last grow. All the girls having been in jars curing for at least 30 days, some longer.

The group consisted of all autos, a Zittlez, Chocolate Skunk, Dark Devil and Purple Lemonade.

 Zittlez 

Really sweet taste. The effect is not that pronounced, but still nice. It affects you, but only to the extent that you know you've smoked "something." I had a major mishap with this one early in the grow, so this review relates to a less than perfectly grown plant. It turned out really stunted but with fat buds. She might be much better if grown without issues. But in this instance, I think she was kind of a middle-of-the-road weed, and, if possible, I don't drive in the middle of the road.

items.name: Genetics, Hermies, Bad Breeding, Autos, and the Destruction of Our Plant
items.name_norm: genetics hermies bad breeding autos and the destruction of our plant
items.thread_title: Genetics, Hermies, Bad Breeding, Autos, and the Destruction of Our Plant
items.grow_notes:
this is a conversation that needs to happen.

my current grow has just destroyed itself in a raging fit of hermie induced seeding mere weeks from finishing what would have been a stellar harvest. while there can be a few causes, it comes at a time when both myself and other growers have noticed a severe uptick in the number of failed grows caused by hermies.

there really is no mystery as to why it is occurring. it's been on the radar for years now in the true medical growing community, and has been a topic at growing seminars locally i have attended. i started hearing about the issue in the early 2010's, and it has increased to the point where it started hitting mainstream consciousness about 5 - 7 yrs ago.

when we grew only regs it was a super rare occurrence. when we started getting femmed photos it could be an occasional problem. when we got autos it became a massive freaking issue and has steadily gotten worse.

autos really need to be outlawed.

the problem is simple, way too many shit breeders banging way too many shit things together, and now most of the genetics breeders need to rely on are crap and compromised.

even decent breeders have difficulty getting clean genetics
items.excerpt:
this is a conversation that needs to happen.

my current grow has just destroyed itself in a raging fit of hermie induced seeding mere weeks from finishing what would have been a stellar harvest. while there can be a few causes, it comes at a time when both myself and other growers have noticed a severe uptick in the number of failed grows caused by hermies.

there really is no mystery as to why it is occurring. it's been on the radar for years now in the true medical growing community, and has been a topic at growing seminars locally i have attended. i started hearing about the issue in the early 2010's, and it has increased to the point where it started hitting mainstream consciousness about 5 - 7 yrs ago.

when we grew only regs it was a super rare occurrence. when we started getting femmed photos it could be an occasional problem. when we got autos it became a massive freaking issue and has steadily gotten worse.

autos really need to be outlawed.

the problem is simple, way too many shit breeders banging way too many shit things together, and now most of the genetics breeders need to rely on are crap and compromised.

even decent breeders have difficulty getting clean genetics to work with. the basement breeders don't care at all. anyone can throw a website together and look as legit and established as anyone else now, and it's destroying the industry.

it's bad enough that self-seeding hermie auto plants are projected be the norm if things don't get cleaned up. straight reg photos with clean genetics are very rare now. fems are worse. it's leading to a world that is no fun to grow in.

a lot of the true medical community here has gone right back to only regs, many are doing it to try preserve what is left. our commercial industry now is breeding not to gain desired traits, but to try to lose bad ones.

most commercial growing for dispensaries in canada are going back to regs to try and get control. hermies in a commercial grow can cause enough damage to negate the year's profits or even put the grower out of business.

we really need professional regulation in the industry. we are at the point if we don't get rid of some the lousy breeding and proliferation of junk autos, we could simply pollute the gene pool to the point it can't be fixed.

even the originator of the auto flower industry believes it is destroying our plant in combination with wild west breeding practices, and how the industry buys and distributes genetics. he touches on it in this podcast :

I really need to write an essay or something on my methods and protocols and vocabulary soon one of these days...

So starting with Mutt history; my first three mutts were all fully and truly unknowns, each one did get grown out, but only 2 had any sort of harvest.

Mutt:00, which for now I will call LBPTCS:0 (Little Brother's Pre Turn of The Century Seed) is what started my journey in growing and gardening in general. He could not remember what the strain was, or even if they knew it back in the day, so that became my very first Mutt.

Due to being a total noob at this, I really screwed up and even neglected it down in the basement grow room too much, to where I just mostly forgot about it and left it for dead. Come Spring or Summer the next year (2016), we were remembered finally, and pulled the remains from the grow room. The little bugger had actually flowered and made buds during that period, about 1/10 ounce, which gave enough for a couple 5 puff huffs from the little toker. and it did give a buzz. So I went ahead and retroactively dubbed that one Necro:2016.

After that, I started another seed, LBPTCS:1, from the same batch Dave handed over to me in 2015. That became Mutt:01. Due to some unexpected late Spring freezes, she went hermie on me down in the grow room, and was discarded. That was Mutt:01, which even though it was never harvested or pollen collected, is known retroactively as Hermie:2017. I do recall having a few more seeds from that batch that I tried out, but they fizzled out after a while for one reason or another (mostly my own derpiness and inexperience), but do not have any surviving records of any of them, and thus won't be adding them to this list.

Mutt:02 was an "opportunity seed" from 2017 found in some weed given me by my neighbor, who moved out end of 2022. Like with the PTC seeds, there were a small few, but only one makes the list here, since the others did not survive long and I can't remember them clearly enough. Anyway, I call this mutt NCMT:0 (Neighbor Cam Mutt). It grew big and beautiful after going in the cage June 2018, and grew out to make its buds. Unfortunately, we made the mistake of trusting weather reports and panicked, harvesting way too early when it looked like there were a few too many early freezes on the way. She produced no seeds (so not even self pollinated, unless I missed a seed or two during processing), and the bud was adequate, but still total weak sauce. I called that Early Bird:2018. I actually still have a small baggie of the bud, mostly ground up now; which I occasionally hit for some additional variety; and it does seem to have become a little better after 6 years. I have that stuff now labeled as Hot Dog Meat.

Those were the initial mutts that at least helped me get my feet wet.. And all three were assigned the pet project name of Feyleaf. That name is now restricted to whatever the Primary (Subject:00) for my Feyleaf strain.

I had one mutt last year, designated Mutt:03 - Guttersnipe:07 / 2022. It was found among the sunflowers off the west end of my porch.

 Royal Queen Seeds Description​ In the words of Epictetus: "Nothing great is created suddenly". It took lots of experimentation and tweaking by the Tyson 2.0 team to create a strain worthy of such a title. As the potent progeny of Gelato 44 and Cookies Auto, GOAT'lato Auto will go down as a hall-of-famer thanks to her euphoric high and rapid growing speed.

GOAT'lato Auto: Destined for Greatness

 RQS has entered Mike Tyson’s corner. Through an exclusive collaboration with Tyson 2.0, we’re making his favourite strains available in seed form. Find out why GOAT’lato Auto marijuana seeds deserve a place in your grow room or garden.

GOAT’lato Auto: The Successor of Gelato 44 & Cookies Auto

When future generations look back at Gelato genetics, GOAT’lato Auto will certainly rank as one of the Greatest Of All Time. Much of the success of this champion cultivar boils down to her legendary parent strains. Gelato 44 passed down boatloads of scrumptious terpenes, whereas Cookies Auto infused the progeny with speedy growing times.

Effects, Flavours, and Aromas of GOAT’lato Auto: Sweet and Relaxing

The GOAT’lato Auto weed strain pulls no punches when it comes to its effect. A seemingly moderate THC content of 20% synergises with saccharine terpenes to produce a deeply relaxing and euphoric high that fills the most menial of tasks with the excitement of a title fight. As she sends waves of relaxation pulsing across the body, her aromatic chemicals target the taste buds with flavours of cookies, fruit, and earthiness.

Growing Characteristics of GOAT’lato Auto Seeds

Left to her own devices, GOAT’lato Auto becomes a bulky heavyweight. However, growers can easily facilitate a weight cut using different training techniques to keep her small and light. Indoor plants grow to 70–120cm and produce up to 450g/m². In contrast, outdoor plants peak at a height of 160cm and are capable of producing up to 180g/plant. This speedy strain cruises through her entire growing cycle in as little as 10 weeks, making her ideal for those seeking a quick stash.

items.grow_notes:
Learn all about RQS ' Granddaddy Purple strain, a refreshing take on the Californian classic and an all-rounder that promises to please. 

Heralded as a true Californian Classic, the Granddaddy Purple strain features an outstanding lineage and over twenty years of refinement. In fact, the beautiful coloration and intense stone have captured the hearts of smokers and growers worldwide. Keen cultivators love to watch the deep purple hues take hold, while smokers can't wait to get their hands on the impressive potency.

To understand what makes Granddaddy Purple so desirable, you must first examine the strains responsible for passing on potency, growing vigor, flavor, and more. In this case, Royal Queen Seeds enlisted the help of Purple Urkle and Big Bud. The former is another Californian OG with abundant skunk and berry flavors alongside a deeply physical high. The latter is the three-way offspring of Afghani, Northern Lights and Skunk #1, an iconic blend of genetics that helped Big Bud rise to fame in Dutch coffeeshops during the 1980s.

items.name: Growing Apple Betty from Herbies Seeds
items.name_norm: growing apple betty from herbies seeds
items.thread_title: Growing Apple Betty from Herbies Seeds
items.grow_notes:
Greetings,

Seem to be quite a bit of interest in this strain lately !

 Apple Betty @HerbiesSeeds 

This is an abridged version of my journey up to today. 134 days total, 81 days of flower 

A couple of weeks over their guesstimate, he, he.. 

Full grow in my signature....

I germinated one seed in a shot glass with about an ounce of distilled water and a spritz of Hydrogen Peroxide.

Glass placed in a Tupperware container on my kitchen table, 48 hours later we have lift off !

Placed in a yogurt/solo cup a finger nail deep with ProMix HP and moistened with a solution of .7g/gallon of MC one part.

When the cup starts to feel "light" I water until run off, slowly around the edges. Wet/dry right from the start. 

Well water, no pH down and no Cal/Mag 

Before I had my light to plant height worked out she was likely 3" high. I simply mounded the medium around her to support her.

Transplanted at day 17, sprinkled the root ball with DYNOMYCO C Mycorrhizal Fungi and placed in a prepared hole in a 5 gallon fabric bag of dampened ProMix HP.

items.excerpt:
Hey all, first time posting here so if anyone sees things i could improve on and/or fix please don't hesitate! I'm a very open book and love criticism as that's what makes you better.

 So anyway heres a layout : I'm currently growing inside of a 1.5 x 1.5 x 2.0 tent, using a Digi-lumen 400w LED full spectrum, a vivosun aerozesh 4" inline fan attached to a matching carbon filter of same brand (bought in bundle), 2x 4" circulator fans vivosun brand, 4x 27L (7 gallon) pots with a 50/50 coco blend in the Widows and a coco blend from the local shop in the skywalkers pot (trying 2 types to test, no specific reason really), a 180w heat bar attached to thermostat and a Vivosun aerostream H19 humidifier. 

Before this current setup i was using a DWC kratky method which i opted to swap out for due to many reasons but as i received great advice from a fellow on here I've changed to the above mentioned method instead using coco and pots.

 Backstory : So i started off with 6x white widow auto seeds purchased from Sacred seeds and soaked them for 24 hours in demineralized water then moved to paper towel to germinate. This was my first attempt at growing since 5+ years ago and back then this method was awesome for me, but sadly hasn't been too great this time. in the first 2 days i had 1 of them burst and grew a 3cm taproot, while another seemed to be going well as was just popped out and had 5mm taproot so only small. The rest stayed in seed. 

At that time i transferred the big one into a small 100mmx100mm plastic net pot and started it inside bucket 1 of the DWC setup.

Few days went by and the 2nd seed that was doing well seemed ready to move into a pot so i did so and had 2x DWC pots going, the other 4x still had no movements. This was about day 4-5

3 more days went by and thats when i opted to swap to coco and pots. Transfer went well and using the same size plastic pots but sitting on top of the 27L coco blend pots until ready to go into the big ones. That's when the other 4x seeds began to show life and could see the seeds split a little and show some white of the taproot.

Another days went by and when checked the seeds again they had begun to turn brow and had grown rot. One of the 4 did seem like it may be savable so i gambled and planted it inside a pot to see if i could rescue it, but sadly it failed. So that brings me to the smaller one of the 2x i had in pots, this one had begun to curl its root back up to the fingers which was odd (seen when moving from paper towel to pots) so i wasn't expecting much from this one if anything at all and my main focus was on the big one that was going strong.

That was about 6 days ago now and currently the big one is about 2.5cm tall and going hard, while the other is still the same size as when i transplanted and slowly seems like it is dying.

After this i visited my local shop and was given 2x clones of skywalker OG that were 2-3 weeks old, and boy the difference is crazy between mine at 1.5 weeks and this at 2-3 weeks. but there clones so they had a head start haha

Currently the water is demineralized water mix with dual fuel 1+2 and pro-Cal from the greenfingers range. and the light schedule is 18/6.

So far they seem to be thriving (except the small one that seems to be getting smaller each day (one leaf turned brown so cut it off as recommended by a local) bare in mind I'm just trying anything to see if it works.

I've now decided i will germinate directly into the pots of coco any new seeds i get and see how that goes. 

Photos will be added in next comment to show my previous DWC setup, and then my current setup now.

have air pulling from top back left into tent and out of the bottom front right pocket to a filter outside tent.

 Notes : Shifted the humidifier from outside to inside as it kept dripping water excess into the pots and didn't want that.

So far they've had a water yesterday and pots still wet. Used a total of 12litres mixed with the ratio given on the greenfingers

"I know alot of people are looking for CBD genetics and there's alot of misleading information. Here's a collection of different strains that all claim to contain CBD.

This is by no means conclusive or correct, just a list I wanted to compile... almost all copy and paste.

Feel free to add any strains or descriptions and correct any mistakes...."

high CBD strains (above 4% CBD)

 clones with names 

Harlequin-

Harlequin is one phenotype of a plant bred to produce hashish. The genes are 75% sativa and 25 % indica. The Sativas include an early-1970s Columbian Gold, a Thai from the mountains near Laos, and a Swiss native land race that was bred for consumption of cattle. The Indica is from Nepal's Mustang state. These are all high-elevation plants... Harlequin is available as a clone at dispensaries in the Bay Area that are participants in Project CBD, including Sparc and the Vapor Room. The smell and taste are sweet with an almost syrupy heaviness that is pleasant on the inhale and the exhale. she needs about 60 to 70 days indoors to finish her full flowering. She sets flowers fairly quickly compared to other strains. I see fingertip-sized bud set at two weeks of flower - compared to pencil-eraser size in other plants at the same two weeks of flower. She really needs some way to support the colas the last few weeks because the trichomes and flowering tops get so heavy. Along those same lines, in a drying room where strains like Blueberry or Bubba Kush take seven to 10 days for drying before curing, the Harlequin can take as long as three weeks. She can be completely obscured by 'sugar' to where she looks “frosted".

Harlequin has a CBD:THC ratio that is almost always 5:2. That is because the primary phenotype (dominate 50% of the time) is indeed a high CBD strain, unlike most well known CBD strains where the high CBD is a rare/recessive phenotype (Sour Tsunami, etc).

When something is synergistic, by definition, the overall effect is greater than the sum of the parts. For most patients, a near 50/50 mix of CBD and THC is MUCH better at controlling pain than either CBD or THC by itself. ‘Near’ 50/50 would include 75/25, and Harlequin fits that criteria very well. In terms of brain tumor growth, scientific studies have shown that both CBD and THC have about equal effects on tumor cells. The same studies have shown that a 1:1 ratio of CBD:THC has a much greater effect than either used separately; another example of synergy.

Perkins Cut-

Cannatonic

---- up to 20.2% CBD and 23% total cannabinoids.

Sativa dominant phenotype. Smell has an extra sharp kick of sour/citrusy funk. It typically yields about 6 zips per plant with a 2 week veg in my garden in DWC

Much respect due to Huel Perkins paying it FWD!

ACDC-

See Cannatonic.

Pheno found by Dr. Courtney. 20% CBD

"This strain is very hard to grow. A light feeder. High on the pH also.

She smells of blue velvety perfume. If left to go past ten weeks flowering she begins to get a touch skunky and purple. She smokes as smooth as you'd want. But it is just not thick on the lungs. Ac/dc makes a fantastic oil! The high is racy. Your heart rate speeds up and you get eager a touch. This settles after ten minutes.

Almost No Thc high feeling at all. Fantastic daytime smoke." -Jefe Noche

Valentine X-

Valentine is a 50/50 Sativa/Indica hybrid mix. It is a phenotype of ACDC and is closely related. We have run lab tests to see if it was actually different than ACDC, and the terpene print is different, but fairly close.

Oracle-

see Cannatonic

items.excerpt:
<Rant, Rage, and Bitch mode = ON >

I recently ordered seeds from two different vendors and both managed to make it to me…eventually. Both came in generic packaging with nothing suggesting the contents. The orders were small ones compared to orders I’ve read about on the forum. Each order had roughly 15-20 seeds in them..all were three-packs except one which was a five pack. I really just wanted to try several varieties to see what worked out for me and then settle on two or three strains. I’m not a heavy smoker these days but have a new interest in tincture. 

Well, I had been tracking my last order and arriving home yesterday I stopped in the driveway just off the road to check it’s delivery status. I live in a rural area and it said the package would be to me in like 3 minutes! I looked down the road about a half mile and saw the rural letter carriers jeep stopped at my neighbors’s mailbox. I waited but she was there for several minutes so I drove on up to the house and went inside.

About ten minutes later i checked the delivery status again and it said the package was in the mailbox!!! Yippie!!!! I walked down to the mailbox to excitedly retrieve the package…I opened the door on the mailbox and there it was!!!…an invisible box of seeds!!! The mailbox was EMPTY!!! I quickly thought about it and knew I had to act quickly. I drove down to my neighbor’s mailbox and peeked inside. There were several packages stuffed in there. But, I knew mine would be a small box. On top of the wadded-up soft “bagged” packages that were stuffed in the mailbox was a small, thin brown box. I felt like a regular a notorious federal criminal but I carefully pulled the box out and, sure enough, it had my name on it! So, I sat the little box on the console and drove over to my neighbor’s house and told them what had transpired. 

It’s not the first time packages have been delivered wrongly to them or to us. Anyhow, I got them before they could have “accidentally” been opened. The neighbors are good people, but one *may* be an auxiliary deputy sheriff…thus my urgency in getting the package. There’s nothing the seed vendor could have done to prevent this from happening except for maybe printing my address larger/bolder…but, I’m not sure even that would have mattered. I really have zero respect for the USPS these days…

items.excerpt:
Strain Mix: Lemon Skunk & GG#4 (including the "Runt")

 Current Stage: Early Veg / Post-Transplant

 Location: 4x4 Basement Tent (Integrated with Blue Dream clones)

- seedlings were previously in an AC Infinity humidity dome since April 19, 2026 , after soaking them starting the evening of the 18th.

 1. Transplant Milestone: May 4, 2026 ​ Time of Move: 11:30 AM – 12:00 PM ET

 Vessels: 1-Gallon Fabric Pots

 Medium: "Lasagna" Build (Pro-Mix base with layered Gaia Green/Northeast Worms Cocktail)

 Execution Notes: ​ 
 The "Bare Root" Transition: Upon removal of the Jiffy mesh, dry soil fell away from several root balls. This allowed for 100% direct application of Mykos to the roots. 
 Mykos Protocol: "Double-Dusting" performed. Generous application directly to the exposed root balls and into the base of the excavated "dummy holes." 
 The "Bury Deep" Maneuver: Stems were successfully buried up to approximately 0.5" from the first set of leaves to establish a stable, subterranean root base. 
 Hydration: Watered in with Recharge (1.5 tsp/gal dose). Approximately 0.5 gallons of the solution was shared between the six new transplants and the Blue Dream clones to prime the microbial workforce. 
 2. Recovery Phase & Environment ​ 
 Recovery Nap: Lights out at 12:00 PM ET. Plants entered a 6-hour dark period to minimize transplant shock and prioritize root establishment over photosynthesis. 
 Integrated Light Cycle: Synced to 6:00 PM – 12:00 PM (18/6 cycle). 
 Target Intensity: Level 4 (Samsung EVO 480W). 
 Target Climate: 73° F / 73% rH (Steady). 
 3. Observations & Upcoming Goals ​ 
 The Runt: Received a higher concentration of Mykos to boost its development and help it catch up to the more aggressive Lemon Skunks. 
 Blue Dream Status: Received a primer dose of Recharge today; ready for the Gaia Green 4-4-4 / 2-8-4 top-dress scheduled for later this week. 
 Watch List: 
 Turgor Pressure: Check for "praying" leaves at 6:00 PM sunrise. 
 Neon Growth: Anticipating a shift in leaf color/vigor by Wednesday/Thursday as roots hit the "Treasure Chest" layer. 
 Humidity: Monitor AC Infinity controller for spikes due to the addition of six damp 1-gallon pots.

items.grow_notes:
Few strains have made as much of an impact in the UK scene as Stardog (aka Stardawg) . This legendary sativa-dominant hybrid is one of our consistent top 5 sellers — and for good reason.

 Genetics & Background 

Stardog comes from a powerhouse lineage: Chemdawg #4 x Tres Dawg , two classics that combine to deliver potency, flavour, and resilience. Double Seeds have refined this variety into one of the best versions available today.

 Why Collectors Love Stardog 

 
 THC: Up to 24% (very high) 
 Ratio: 90% Sativa / 10% Indica 
 Flowering Time: 56–63 days (around 8–9 weeks) 
 Indoor Yield: 550–700 g/m² 
 Outdoor Yield: Up to 800 g/plant 
 Aroma & Flavour: Earthy pine with sharp diesel and a twist of lemon 
 Appearance: Bright green buds with fiery orange hairs and dense, popcorn-like structure 
 

 Effects Profile 

Stardog is known for its uplifting, energetic, and often giggly high , paired with a mellow body relaxation. Collectors prize it for its long-lasting potency, with effects that can stretch up to 3 hours.

items.excerpt:
"Heirloom And Landrace Cannabis Strains"

by Rick Pfrommer, Director of Education, Harborside Health Center 

Original landrace and other heirloom strains are often lost in today’s hyperkinetic world of breeding. ‘Landrace’ refers to strains that are indigenous to an area, such as Red Congolese. ‘Heirlooms’ are strains that were collected worldwide during the 1970s and propagated in Hawaii and Northern California. Our constant desire for new strains leads breeders to continually cross and re-cross existing strains looking for the next big thing. There is, however, a small but growing contingent of cultivators who’re returning to our cannabis roots and propagating old landrace and heirloom strains. Varieties range from pure African sativas to Afghani indicas, collected by world travelers on the infamous Hippie Trail (also referred to as the “Hashish Trail”).

All during the 1970s and early 1980s, cannabis aficionados of all stripes traveled the world smoking the finest cannabis and hashish available. From Nepalese temple balls to the famed Mazar-i-Sharif Afghani Black, the Hashish Trail was filled with exotic delights. The trail rolls on through Lebanese Red to Moroccan Kif, with stops in Bangkok for Chocolate Thai, and Columbia and Mexico for their infamous golden strains. Many of these intrepid souls also collected seeds during their travels. It was these landrace strains that became the basis for the nascent cultivation culture that eventually sprang forth in both Hawaii and Northern California.

Talk with any cannabis connoisseur old enough to remember these legendary strains and you’ll come away with tales of their epic strength. Equatorial sativas from Africa to Vietnam flourished in Hawaii’s tropical dreamscape of cannabis cultivation. Indicas from Afghanistan were more at home in Northern California’s cooler climate. I was fortunate enough to live on the Big Island of Hawaii from 1993 to 1997, and I can attest that the best cannabis I have EVER smoked was grown in volcanic soil on the slopes of the largest active volcano in the world, Mauna Loa. By the time I got there almost everything grown in Hawaii was some combination of genetics, no longer a landrace. Yet a few of the old-timers still had access to the classic ’70s strains, making for a wonderfully unique and diverse smoking experience.

From Nepalese temple balls to the famed Mazar-i-Sharif Afghani Black, the Hashish Trail was filled with exotic delights. 

The scene in California at this time was slightly different. Northern California, as beautiful as it is, ain’t Hawaii. The Emerald Triangle rests approximately on the same parallel as Afghanistan and the Hindu Kush mountains. While Southern Californians could grow Columbian and Mexican sativas, their northern counterparts found the stocky indica plants much better adapted for their climate. Shorter flowering time allowed harvest to occur before the fall rains came with their mold-inducing downpours. These short and chunky plants produced the infamous skunkweed that became Northern California’s calling card. Again, anyone old enough to remember this cannabis will never forget the pungent, almost rancid, skunk-like aroma. I remember going to parties in the early ’80s with this herb double-bagged-and still being outed minutes after walking in. “Yo man, I know you’re holding, share the love!” Our own Steve DeAngelo also has memories of this era, saying that to this day he’s not seen cannabis like what he saw from Northen California in the late ’70s and early ’80s.

So what does all this nostalgia mean for modern patients and cannabis aficionados? Well, several breeders have also recognized the value in these old-school strains. Ace Seeds, CannaBioGenn, Reeferman Seeds and Tom Hill, as well as the one-and-only Neville, are all selling a wide variety of landrace and heirloom seeds. Look for some of these to be available at Harborside in the near future. Growers who’re looking for ways to stay ahead of the curve in a

Strain Name - Lemon Drop Haze

From - Soma Seeds

When - 3/20

items.grow_notes:
DNA defines this strain as 2 different skunk parents that had strong lemon characteristics. I didnt see lemon in any of the plants i grew. (3 seasons) i did however have a plant that smelled of berries. Funny story, my first season i had 2 plants in RDWC. The " berry" plant i mentioned and a larger plant that smelled of diesel. Both plants together did 27oz. I cant hardly bitch for not getting any lemon.

The taste was decent, but nothing too crazy. It was stoney, but not the last word in strength. 

Its good bud, but it could be better if it were skunky or lemony

items.excerpt:
Hey fellow growers, 

I wanted to start a thread about regular seeds - the OGs of cannabis cultivation. Whether you’re new to the game or a seasoned grower, understanding regular seeds and their role in the grow room is key to mastering this art. Let’s dive in!

 What Are Regular Seeds?​ Regular seeds are as natural as it gets—unaltered seeds with a 50/50 chance of producing either male or female plants. Think of them as the raw building blocks of cannabis breeding.

 Why Grow Regular Seeds?​ Here’s why regular seeds are still a big deal in today’s world of feminized and autoflowering options:

 
 Breeding Potential 

Regular seeds are a must-have if you’re a grower with an itch for creating your strains. You’ll need both male and female plants for pollination, and regular seeds are the only way to that genetic diversity. 
 Stable Genetics 

Regular seeds are often prized for their purity and robustness . They’re less likely to carry genetic quirks that can show up in heavily modified seeds. 
 Back to Basics 

Something is rewarding about cultivating cannabis the way nature intended. Regular seeds offer an opportunity to learn, experiment, and gain a deeper appreciation for the plant. 
 Who Should Use Regular Seeds?​ Regular seeds are ideal for:

 
 Breeders : Crafting new strains or preserving classic genetics. 
 Traditionalists : Those who love the full hands-on growing experience. 
 Growers With Space : You’ll need room to separate the males from the females. 
 Top 3 Selling Regular Seeds on RocketSeeds .com​ 

 1. Afghan Regular Seeds 

A timeless classic, Afghan Regular is known for its earthy aroma and heavy resin production. Perfect for hash enthusiasts or those looking to breed robust indica strains.

items.excerpt:
MAC (Miracle Alien Cookies) by Herbie's Seeds USA. Feminized, photoperiod . @Herbies Seeds 

I was fortunate enough to win the Grow Journal of the Month in November of 2023 and Herbie's Seeds was kind enough to let me pick my strains and give me one extra too, so that I might fill my four hole hydro flood and drain tray. I picked MAC mainly because it was a strain that really impressed me a few years ago while visiting family in Florida. I love the taste and the buzz was real nice too. 

 Here's what Herbie's Seeds USA has to say about MAC 

A very popular descendant of Alien Cookies, Mac is a perfect choice for Indica lovers. She’s insanely high-yielding at 2.1 oz/ft² and has equally astounding THC levels of up to 27%, so you get exactly what you like and you get it big! Expect a burst of euphoria and happiness with every toke, plus a one-of-a-kind flavor profile that combines notes of spice and wood with a citrusy finish.

 Mac Strain Info: 

Mac has all the traits that Indica lovers are looking for both in a plant and in a smoke. With a compact stature and record-breaking yields, she provides the owners of tight grow spaces with more bud than they can use up. Quantity aside, the quality of your harvest will be top-notch too.

 Genetics: 

Mac is short for Miracle Alien Cookies, so it’s obvious which lineage this hybrid carries. We’d rather not reveal her other parent’s identity, but it definitely helped us improve on the original Alien Cookies.

 Flowering Time: 

As is the case with many Indica-dominant varieties, Mac doesn’t take long to finish flowering and u sually matures in 63 days after you switch your timer to 12/12. 

 Yields :

Mac is an incredibly rewarding plant. Give her enough light and some basic love and care, and she’ll reward you with 2.1 oz/ft² (650 g/m²) indoors. Outdoor yields are even more generous at 1.65 lb (750 grams) per plant.

 Effects: 

If you have enough tolerance to stand up to this strain’s potency, you will find this smoke very happy and euphoric, with marked creative vibes – something you’d expect from a Sativa. However, the relaxation typical for Indicas will also be there and will make more inexperienced users motionless and speechless.

 Medical Properties: 

Whatever healing powers you’d expect from Indica weed, you’ll get it all with Mac. It’s a versatile medicine, equally fit to cure both the mind and body. Most often, people use it to improve sleep and treat pains of various origins, including arthritis, headaches, and migraines. However, Mac’s mood-lifting ability also makes it effective against stress, anxiety, and depression.

 THC and CBD Levels: 

Mac is among the most potent hybrids out there, as its THC levels routinely test at 25-27%. This is enough to pierce the armor of almost any tolerance, and even long-time medical patients are not immune. The CBD content isn’t particularly high, cruising below 2%.

 Smell and Taste: 

The terpene profile is complex, featuring a citrusy background resembling something like sweet oranges. However, the main notes on your palate are spicy and woody, with a more subtle earthy taste.

 Grow Tips: 

Mac is a versatile plant that adapts well to any environment and growing style. She’s also very forgiving and will tolerate some lack of attention as well as lack of experience. This makes her suitable for first-time growers, while more seasoned ones will see their extra effort transform into extra yields.

 Expect a medium height of about 3′7″-4′3″ (110-130 cm).

 Strive for a perfectly flat canopy to maximize yields.

 Provide good ventilation to prevent mold in the super-dense buds.

 Time to get going. 

I will start out in plugs

then move into 6"/15cm net pots in a small diy tupperware DWC, until I get a little growth.

then move into their forever home, a four hole flood and drain tray through veg and flower to harvest

Enjoy

Price per 1/4oz: $112

Experience: Heavy Indica stone. Nasal compression. Eyes at half mast, but oh so chilllllllllll...

items.thread_title: Mel Grows Mimosa x Orange Punch from Barney's Farm, Outdoors Comparative Grow
items.grow_notes:
Hi everyone!

I'm joining in on this comparative grow of Mimosa x Orange Punch, from @Barneys Farm !

After a brief indoor interlude to start the seed, I'll be moving her outdoors to brave the elements in Southern Ontario.

I'll be growing her in a rich soil blend, in a 60 litre SIP, and feeding her Mega Crop from @Greenleaf Nutrients .

I'll be training her in my usual octoline style, although I'm making a couple of modifications to (hopefully) avoid some issues that have arisen in the past.

The cool nights we usually get through September into October should help to bring out any possible Autumn colours in her foliage, and while I don't intend to grow a giant again, I make no promises.

With all that out of the way, here's the strain info directly from the Barney's Farm website!

items.excerpt:
Grow Your Own: Six New Strains Available Today to Consumers Globally, With More to Come in Collaboration With Mike Tyson’s Heavy-Hitting Cannabis Brand 

We’ve just taken our next exciting step as one of the world’s largest and most trusted cannabis seed banks! Today, we’re announcing our exclusive partnership with TYSON 2.0, the premium cannabis brand co-founded by cultural icon Mike Tyson. Our collaboration will offer distinct cannabis genetics, to grow from seed, direct to consumers (DTC) and through retail channels across the globe.

Our first 6 strains available starting today— Gelato 44 , Dynamite Diesel , NYC Sour D (autoflower), GOAT'lato Auto , Punch Pie and Corkscrew (autoflower)—are a combination of nostalgic old-school and contemporary genetics, available as feminized and autoflowering seeds that will consistently deliver exceptional home grow experiences. An additional 12 strains are on tap for our three-year partnership.

Since launching Royal Queen Seeds in the U.S. more than a year ago, we have been on the search for a partner who meets and exceeds our expectations in bringing exceptional cannabis products to market; TYSON 2.0 has consistently delivered. We believe that it is everyone’s right to be able to grow cannabis at home, and the seeds we're launching with TYSON 2.0 create top-rate stunners—truly beautiful plants in terms of looks, flavour and effects.

Touching gloves with Tyson was an easy decision, especially considering his personal passion for the plant. As the Co-founder and Chief Brand Officer of TYSON 2.0, Tyson himself has expressed: “Growing my own cannabis has been very important to me. It has been a fundamental principle in my journey to deepen my relationship with the plant.” He’s also impressed with the way we do things, saying: “Growing cannabis at home is an amazing way to slow life down and find enrichment—and the pros with Royal Queen Seeds really know what they’re doing. These first six strains are a perfect taste of what’s to come.”

As a globally award-winning cannabis seed bank operating since 2007, we’re primed to bring genetics with the Tyson seal of approval to cannabis lovers and home growers all across the world through DTC channels, while TYSON 2.0 will utilise its retail network. Additionally, with New Jersey and Washington having filed bills to legalise home grow, and New York being in the midst of regulating home grow, our partnership could see the total addressable market explode over the next year.

 

“Great cannabis flower starts with great genetics,” said Adam Wilks, CEO of Carma HoldCo, the parent company of TYSON 2.0. “Growing cannabis at home has long been a pastime of this community, and our collaboration makes it easy for consumers to know that the seeds they buy make the same high-quality cannabis that Tyson himself expects."

The six exclusive TYSON 2.0 strains are now available in the U.S. (excluding Kansas and Kentucky) and internationally, and can be purchased as one-, three-, five- and 10-seed packs. For online orders and more information, visit www.royalqueenseeds.com/us/tyson20
