items.name: Mimosa Via Symbiotic Genetics - Heavy 16 - Coco - Xmas Run!
items.name_norm: mimosa via symbiotic genetics heavy 16 coco xmas run
items.thread_title: Mimosa Via Symbiotic Genetics - Heavy 16 - Coco - Xmas Run!
items.grow_notes:
Hey all, posting my first grow log here. I'm in week 2 of Veg for my Mimosa run

 
 Symbiotic genetics - Mimosa Reg 
 Coco Medium 
 Heavy 16 nutrients (full line) 
 Plants 4 
 Tent size: 8x4 
 FlexStar 720 Pro for left half 
 AgroMax AFS1830 for right half 
 I typically run ebb and flow buckets, but when trying a new nutrient line I prefer to hand water and dial things in. I like to get a feel for plant uptake and cultivar specific needs with a new line without mixing full res.

I'm about 3 weeks in veg starting this log, I plan on vegging at least two more weeks while I do some additional LST.

I topped them about a week ago and although they bounced back it wasn't as quickly as I'd like to see. 

If anyone has ran Mimosa, has any pointers/tips etc. Please feel free to chime in. Community is about helping your peers and sharing what you learn so we can all grow together. I will keep this main post for my updates and answer questions/chat/etc in the below comments so the grow log remains clean and easy to follow.

 
 - Sept 19/25 - Transplanted clones from solos, leaves lighter than other cultivars - just using clonex with coco while the roots developed - 100 PPFD avg, 92F, 80%RH.
items.excerpt:
Hey all, posting my first grow log here. I'm in week 2 of Veg for my Mimosa run

 
 Symbiotic genetics - Mimosa Reg 
 Coco Medium 
 Heavy 16 nutrients (full line) 
 Plants 4 
 Tent size: 8x4 
 FlexStar 720 Pro for left half 
 AgroMax AFS1830 for right half 
 I typically run ebb and flow buckets, but when trying a new nutrient line I prefer to hand water and dial things in. I like to get a feel for plant uptake and cultivar specific needs with a new line without mixing full res.

I'm about 3 weeks in veg starting this log, I plan on vegging at least two more weeks while I do some additional LST.

I topped them about a week ago and although they bounced back it wasn't as quickly as I'd like to see. 

If anyone has ran Mimosa, has any pointers/tips etc. Please feel free to chime in. Community is about helping your peers and sharing what you learn so we can all grow together. I will keep this main post for my updates and answer questions/chat/etc in the below comments so the grow log remains clean and easy to follow.

 
 - Sept 19/25 - Transplanted clones from solos, leaves lighter than other cultivars - just using clonex with coco while the roots developed - 100 PPFD avg, 92F, 80%RH. 
 - Sept 24/25 - First full feed of Heavy16 - pH 5.7. 10% runoff. 
 Oct 1st - Turned up lights 300 PPFD, plants are moving along. Growth not as explosive as with previous cultivar - This seed to a bit longer than most to grow out and get clones from. It's a slow rooter and somewhat slow out of the gate. This is my first time running Mimosa so I don't have anything to compare it to outside of other coco runs which isn't the best gauge. 
 Oct 2nd - Added microbes for fungus gnat control and IPM purposes. 
 Oct 5th - Swapped out Florflex 700 for FlexStar 720 PRO, matched ppfd of AFS on right side of tent. Both lights at 50% power with a few feet of clearance above the canopy. Avg PPFD - 480. 
 Oct 6th - Started LST, bending a few branches and putting down my tie downs. Since she didn't really bounce back from topping this early I decided to go the LST route for the next week or so then give her another topping once the rootzone has become stronger and the plant shows more vigor.

items.excerpt:
Strain/s : Northern Light Auto

 Genetic Makeup : Indica

 Pot/Bucket Size : 4 Gallon

 Tent Size : 2' x 2' x 4'

 Grow Space : 10' x 15'

 How Many Plants : 1

 Environment : Indoor

 Stage : Vegetative

 Medium : FF Ocean Forest + Extra Perlite

 Lights : 100 Watt LED

 Nutrients : None yet, I'll keep an eye out for nutrient deficiencies

 Room/Tent Temperature : 77F

 Relative Humidity : 76%

 Media/Res pH : about 6.5

 Pests : None

 Watering : when the moisture meter shows the soil is drying (several days right now)

This initially was going to be an outdoor grow, but we've been having a lot of problems with deer, rabbits, and various molds and other plant diseases in our garden so I decided to move it indoors.

Seedling stretched a bit because the lighting wasn't optimal outside for the first couple of days. Had some humidity issues after moving it into the tent which I suspect stalled growth so I got a humidifier with a physical on-switch, then put it on one of the grow controller's managed outlets and set a floor trigger for 75%. The volume of the tent is so small that it's barely turning on to keep the humidity up at 75-78%. I'm planning to lower the trigger to 65% in maybe a week.

Temps are maintaining around 75-80F with the light on, then dropping to low 70s during the 6 hour off period.

With the humidity in range I'm seeing growth again. I think it stalled a few days because of the humidity? Hopefully it won't affect yield a ton. If it does, no big deal, I'll have the correct setup for the next run from the beginning.

Right now I'm at day 16 after germination (and about 14 days after the seedling came up out of the soil).

This is my first grow I've ever done, so I'm expecting mistakes. I'll gradually upgrade my setup across grows.

---

 The Origin of the Journey: From Wheelchair to Grower 

Our story begins in May 2021, the year I was diagnosed with Multiple Sclerosis in an unusually aggressive form. Within six months, I was confined to a wheelchair, unable to eat properly or sleep for more than two hours at a time. When conventional medicine offered no relief, we turned to cannabis. The effects were life-changing: I could sleep again, eat again, and, most importantly, feel joy again.

My medical prescription in Germany also gave me the legal permission to grow my own plants. This was the starting shot for a new passion, but I faced a huge barrier: I am severely disabled and can no longer perform any physical tasks on my own. While my mind was full of ideas, it was my son who became my hands, patiently assembling the tent, wiring the pumps, and turning my digital plans into a physical reality. This project is as much a testament to his support as it is to the technology.

In my search for a control system, I tested and rejected commercial controllers like the Controller 69 Pro, seeing them as „closed golden cages.“ I landed on MacroDroid and an old tablet, giving me the ultimate freedom to innovate.

After 3.5 years of tinkering and countless test runs, we have arrived at the point you see today. When I recently shared this project on Reddit, the response was overwhelmingly positive, and many encouraged me to document the journey in a more permanent format, which has led me here.

This journey is dedicated to everyone who faces physical limitations but refuses to let them define what is possible.

items.excerpt:
Name: Pakistan Chitral Kush

 Breeder: CannaBiogen

 Grown from: Feminized seed

 Grown how: Outdoor organically

 Latitude: 45° N

 Harvested: Between 25th September and 1st October

Pakistan Chitral Kush is a landrace indica strain from Chitral valleys of Pakistan, inbred by Spaniards from CannaBiogen since middle 90's from what I remember. My seed was soaked in water by the end of March and germinated without any problems. After 6 weeks or so the seedling was transplanted to my jungle spot, where it was quickly eaten by some insects (don't ask me which ones). To save the plant, which had only one set of leaves at that point, I had to replant her to a better spot, where it survived and branched out nicely, exactly like I'd have topped it.

Because the soil wasn't prepared there for an extra plant, she grew all natural in marl based loam (that's the type of soil I have here). She was fertilized a little with some bat guano, powdered egg shells and blood meal like the rest of my plants. She survived very wet summer, and only by the end of August she caught septoria as most of my plants did this season. That might've cut into final yield, but didn't really affect anything else. 

Then there was grey mold, which she caught around 3rd week of September after just a little bit of rain. I removed infected budz with scissors and let her keep going, which she did by the end of September/beginning of October, only slightly bothered by bud wormz and more grey mold. But total weight loss was accounted at not more than 5%, so there was no tragedy. Still, definitely not a good strain for humid climates!!!

Before I even got to bud I processed my trim into dry sift hash, which is what I'm leaning to after my few indicas, cause this type of bud cures slowly and usually takes months before it peaks. And here a real character of this strain shows, reminiscent of famous black Afghan hash, if someone still remembers it, which tastes exactly like hash from this strain. Extremely spicy and aromatic it caused immediate coughing and almost immediate relaxation. It put a big smile on my face and let me lay on the couch watching my favorite TV series or a movie. In my opinion it's better than most of Afghan strains on the market, it's livelier and last slightly longer, I'd say up to 1,5 or 1,45. Excellent nighttime strain!

 Smell in early/middle flowering: Musky

 Smell in late flowering: Nutmeg with a touch of pine

 Smell after drying and very short curing: Earthy and aromatic, but slightly sweet like cinnamon

 Taste of hash: Extremely spicy like nutmeg, bordering with burnt rubber

 Taste of bud: Very pleasant and aromatic, a little bit spicy but in a good way

 High: Very relaxing and happy stone, but with some nice introspective quality

 Rating: Solid genetics, so A

 Medicinal use: Doesn't work for my back pain straight away, but the next day after I feel great

After being eaten by insects

items.excerpt:
Producing Feminized Seeds Using Colloidal Silver 

If you want quick information while this journal is in progress, please feel free to review the brief article I submitted: How to Use Colloidal Silver to Produce Feminized Seeds It included some images from my first positive results in using this method.

 This journal will include start to finish photos of both auto-flowering AND non-auto strains. 

Okay... before I even start this, I hope everyone will be understanding if I don't have a lot of time to respond in detail to comments. I love you ALL and SOOOOO appreciate 420magazine giving us this area to share with others, but I don't have much time for getting in here to document. So, my apologies from the git-go if I don't respond to each message individually, but instead group my responses to all of you. I feel bad when I can't respond to each individual... just know I LOVE YA ALL!!!

 PURPOSE: My purpose of even doing another journal is to document my entire process of producing female seeds using Colloidal Silver to hopefully help others to learn how to do this ... and hopefully this will be a productive venture for female seeds for me! 

 INTRO 

I see this trend from seed companies to sell strictly feminized seeds, many strains with no regular seeds available. It makes me wonder if this is due to the increased cost (their profit) for feminized seeds, or if it is also because it reduces their customers from creating more seeds on their own (keeps customers coming back), or maybe it is also because most of their current customer's are preferring female seeds so they don't have to waste time/space/expense in weeding out the males.

Regardless of their reasons, I found the cost astronomical for the return. This last year, I decided to try auto-flowering strains. Auto-flowering plants can't be cloned, so what you get is what you get and they are not large producers - both combining to make seed costs per return very low when compared to non-auto plants that grow large and can be cloned repeatedly (one non-auto seed returns MUCH MORE TO UNLIMITED!).

However, auto flowering plants are SO WONDERFUL for other reasons. They are small, mainly single cola plants so they don't take up much space. They don't depend upon the light cycle - which makes them wonderful strains to add. They have also been around long enough that they have been bred to be much stronger in THC levels than early auto flowering strains - equivalent to the strongest non-auto flowering strains now-a-days.

When I figured out the differences (and that I couldn't clone the autos), I was a bit disappointed. I decided I would produce my own seeds, buying some regular seeds and pollinating with the best male. I figured out quickly that the auto strains I was most interested in didn't offer regular seeds - they offered feminized seeds only. This left me to choose one strain that offered regular seeds to be able to get a male to cross with all the different auto-flowering strains I had. Not what I preferred (wanted pure stains), but would at least get me high quality regular seeds.

I don't know about you folks, but I sure do prefer feminized seeds - even tho they cost a lot more than regular seeds. They sure do save time, expense, and much needed space in the grow room if you don't have to weed out the males.

After ordering more seeds, I got to thinking about it and decided to research how the seed growers produce female seeds. It appeared there were three main ways.

1) Stress the plant to make it grow female pollen sacs.

2) Growing past it's harvest time causing them to throw a few female pollen sacs.

3) Use Colloidal Silver to cause the plant to grow female pollen sacs.

Of those choices, it appeared CS could consistently produce female pollen sacs while the others were not at all consistent.

Below, I will copy the info from the article I posted so I don't have to repeat these instructions, they I will continue with my beginning...

items.excerpt:
Hi Everyone,

My first strain review. I've always been a strain hound. Now that I grow, it's gotten worse. Lmao. I also am in contact with several buddies who grow in one form or another. This is my review of RAINBOW RUNTZ, which I just got from a grower friend of mine - his current crop.

 Strain Name - Rainbow Runtz

 From - A fellow grower who grew this from feminized seeds from Exotic Genetix in soil under LEDs in a 10x10 grow room

 When - He harvested the last week of January. Dried and cured total of almost five weeks before coming to me. Got this today, 3/2/21

 Price - Irrelevant in this case but this is certainly $50+/eighth weed if it were sold in the dispensaries here. Think $400 oz.

 Type - Sativa leaning hybrid that is a cross of Rainbow Chip x Runtz. Apparently this is one of those strains where more than one breeder chose the same name. I hate when that happens. Anyway, this particular review is on the strain as described.

 Appearance - Colors are lots of purple, deep dark green, a silvery trichome-y sheen, some red, and various other shades of green. It is FROSTY with trichomes. The buds are dense - not insanely so but good, solid density. Dense enough that you definitely want to grind them, and you want the trichomes in the base of your grinder. My friend did an experienced job on the dry and cure and pretty much brought out the best in this bud to my eyes.

 Smell - WHOA the smell. Two worlds here: One - pre grind, in bud form - the smell from the bag is immediately strong, pungent, dank, fruity, and primarily lemony/citrusy. Two - post grind - this is where the magic happens. The smell is EXTREMELY fruity, VERY sweet, with a significant sourness in the background to it, and honestly it smells EXACTLY AND PRECISELY like when you open a box of Fruity Pebbles cereal. No joke. That's just exactly what it smells like ground up. Strong strong smell. When I opened the bag my roommate was at my door (I'm at the whole other end of the house) within minutes telling me to take that shit outside. Ha!

 Taste -Again, WHOA. This may be this strain's finest hour. I expected lots of sweetness and fruit, and it has that in droves. But when smoked, at least to my palette, the sourness comes more forward. In a really really good way. It balances the sweetness and brings a serious complexity to the fruit element. Where upon smelling in the bag it seemed primarily lemony, and upon grinding primarily fruity/sweet, upon smoking I got all kinds of specific fruit notes. Lemon for sure. That's the strongest flavor but not overwhelmingly so at all. Well balanced with a combination of a decent amount of orange, a little grape, a little grapefruit, a little peach (!), and maybe a tiny twinge of apple even, although that may have been my wishful thinking. The taste to me was much much more complex than I thought it would be.

 Smoke - I smoked from a clean bong with cold bottled water. The smoke is dense and creamy. Not at all harsh. I was able to take very large hits without a cough from the smoke itself. It's smooth. It's also expansive, and that did get me once. Lol. Great, enjoyable on the palette smoke that is smooth enough to blow out of your nose, which I do to help me gauge the taste. Out of the nose it even gives you a small peppery element, very subtle. The smoke itself is not quite white either - just a slight shade of cream off of regular white. Interesting.

 Type of Buzz - Quick background - I am partially paralyzed from the waist down and have a ton of various back pains. I always was a smoker anyway, but as a result of managing my back pain I am a daily day and night smoker for the last five years. My tolerance is very high, and my personal preference leans sativa or sativa heavy hybrids by a mile. So I say that because "type of buzz" is really "type of buzz as it affected me personally." Cuz this one is different for everyone, right? So from a pothead point of view , the buzz is pretty well balanced and leans strongly

#23-Sweet & Sour D~ Colombia, Mexico & Afghanistan (Sativa Dom Hybrid) 

Sour D x Sour D/Mango Haze - Mom a pure Sour D was collected from an elbow of flowers over Xmas of 99/2000 this came from the infamous upstate crew that hoarded cuts like a pirate and scoured their lbs. for seed like a squirrel, but nobody is perfect and one got through. Just recently realized I do not have a journal for Woofle Dust , and it is only covered in the Tokens journal ( Timing Studies ). Figured it time to rectify that. Woofle Dust is the product of what I call a breedback, where two lite siblings did the dirty and made a new "pure" and triggering a name and claim. My personal rules for naming a breedback is to default to the original name, but increment the progenitor plant by 1. Or alternatively, go thematic. For this, I went thematic...from a particular point of view.

These were produced when my S:02 Feyleaf Lite girl, and S:01 Feyleaf Lite boy did the dirty. In this case, I continued the Fae theme (Woofles are sorta my little Fae creation, with probably a very short and boring origin story...)

items.thread_title: Ravenplume Grow Journal 2025-14 - Wildlings
items.grow_notes:
2025/11/10 - 00:00 

 Time to consolidate all of my Wildlings into a single Wildling journal, in the same way all the Guttersnipe-Mutts go into a single journal. There are a lot now; so far, I am up to Wildling:28/2025 , and it will likely take some time to find all my old journal entries and compile the relevant material into this one journal.

 First off, I will try my best here to define what makes a Wildling. A Wildling is the offspring of any Lite, Guttersnipe, or other Wildling and anything not a sibling, cousin, parent, or other direct lineage. In other words, Wildlings are bred wild and not via "noble breeding" which is my alternate name for inbreeding, which is how "pures" are made. Oh, and the mother plant can not be a pure herself, as breeding a pure with anything other than another pure of the same strain makes a Lite. So here are the Wildlings I have generated so far, and how they came about, with pics of examples where possible.

 Wildling:00/2019 - TK:418 - Tardis Lite 2018 Female + Sour Banana Sherbert Lite 2018 Male

Wildling:01/2023 - TK:419 - Guttersnipe-Mutt 07:03/2023 Female + Unknown Mutt Male/2023 (Free Love Pollination)

Wildling:02/2024 - TK:420 - Guttersni

Welcome aboard.. Everyone is welcome to take a seat This is my second soil grow in like 10-15 years - or, oh well, it's at least many joints ago. And I have been more into hydro (DWC/Drip) over the years. But these days I'm doing soil instead. And it goes like this:

 Strain/s: Anesia's Gigabrain Auto

 Genetic Makeup: 55% Indica (Mendo Breath Auto x First Lady)

 Pot/Bucket Size: ~3 Gallon / 10 liters

 Tent Size: ~3' x 3'/ 1m x 1m

 How Many Plants: 2

 Environment: Indoor

 Stage: Seedling stage

 Medium: ~25% Perlite + 75% Champost potting soil

 Lights: ~300 Watt full spectrum LED

 Nutrients: General Organics + Terra Auqatica

 Room/Tent Temperature: Lights on: ~22-24C : Lights off: ~18-20C

 Relative Humidity: ~40-50%

 Media/Res pH : Unknown

 Pests: None

 Watering: Once Daily / Every other day

So, two plants. One broke the soil yesterday. Now I'm waiting for the other one, fingers crossed, knock, knock, knock..

Hey y'all! Renaissance Man coming back at ya with a detailed grow journal. I threw my hat in the ring for this comparative grow and was one of the 50 selected. I'm looking forward to watching this forum, in fact, it will probably be the only forum I follow for a while given all my favorite growers I've been following over the past few years are participating. 

 

Here's the dealy-o of my setup. I ordered another small tent and exhaust fan. With my other Viparspectra light (P1000), I will now set up a new veg tent (small 2'x2') and the larger flower tent (2'x4' with Viparspectra XS2000). I'll most likely be growing in 5gal fabric pots, but might throw one in a 7 gal for giggles.

 

I have already started a Northern Lights strain and because I have been wanting to do this for a while, instead of culling it, I've decided to grow them together somehow. Less emphasis on the Northern Lights, of course, as this journal will only be showcasing the Barney's Farm Mimosa x Orange Punch.

 

I will be growing in an all organic, soil media using Roots Organic dry amendments (I don't hear too much about in these forums) along with some alpaca manure and worm castings from my worm bin. Typically, I'll make an aerated compost tea also, a couple of times through veg. I also have made my own DIY calmag using eggshells, apple cider vinegar and some molasses that I add. I think my nutrient line has enough cal and mag, but it didn't seem to hurt during my previous grow.

 

I've never ran two tents before and was wondering if I can somehow link the exhaust together or would two 4" exhaust fans, not accomplish much? 

 

Waiting for seeds to arrive and hope to pop in soil on 4/20.

 

This comparative grow is going to be lit!

Your order appears to be shipped due to a website error, we were preparing your order but our system doesn't accept your address.

We are getting this error message:

 An error occurred while validating an address: Address Not Found 

Would you have some apartment number etc to add for your address? We can also use Po box address if you have.

Best regards,

I sent upwards to 3 emails asking for a refund, days apart, no response back. They didnt even notify me they were having issues. When i placed the order, I put my apartment number.

This order was placed and paid for on November 6th 2025, today is November 11th 2025.

items.name: Royal Queen Seeds Orion F1
items.name_norm: royal queen seeds orion f1
items.thread_title: Royal Queen Seeds Orion F1
items.grow_notes:
Royal Queen Seeds Orion F1 

Original Blue Dream is excellent, but this strain goes a step further with the addition of Amnesia

The flavour is similar, rich berry & pine, but Orion has a slightly menthol undertone like toothpaste, very clean and refreshing

There is no thump really, creepy-uppy and quite sedative

My run took quite a while to cold cure and it didn't smell too promising, but after 6-8 weeks, I'm now getting the full Monty of flavours and a very mellow smoke with just a little heady kick

 @Royal Queen Seeds have produced yet another top-notch strain and I'm very glad I still have some seeds - Thank you RQS 

This is knocking on the door of 9/10 for me

items.grow_notes:
Got involved with a seed vendor (supposedly) called Sofem Genetics. He had an auction for seed packs. There were no minimums or reserves announced so I bid on a few packs. The guy comes back and says to me he can award the packs to me at the minimum cost of $25 each vs my bid of $5 & $10 on 3 - 5 packs. I asked him where in the post or auction did it state a reserve, nowhere. 

I offered him $60 for 3 out of the 5 and he just ignored the response and gave me some excuse of "well you should ask first". I don't know about anyone else, but I know auctions and they always have terms up, this one didn't. Just a heads up stay away from this guys auction, you aren't getting anything if he doesn't like the offer, even if there are no other bids. Stay away from SoFem Genetics Auctions.

Description: Seedsman

Black Sugar is an 80% indica strain that develops a round, bushy structure with strong lower branches. It has a short flowering time, a good yield and a typically indica effect. It is a 3-way cross of Black Domina x L.A. OG x Critical.

This plant grows well outdoors as well as indoors due to its robust nature. Its range of cultivability is quite large due to the short flowering period - it is ready to harvest in the northern hemisphere at the end of September or early October at the very latest. In this environment it can grow to be 250 - 300 cm. tall with yields of 800 gr/plant. Indoors flowering will only take 50 - 55 days with superb yields of 600 gr/m2.

Black Sugar has a very fruity lemon and orange taste with pronounced skunk notes. THC levels are very high with low CBD giving an effect that is powerfully narcotic and an exceptional strain with which to relax and do nothing but dream.

Parental lines Black Domina X L.A. OG X Critical Kush

Sex Feminized

Yield outdoor Very High (>750gr/Plant)

Yield indoor High (450-600gr/M2)

Plant height Medium (100-200cm)

Bud density (1=loose & leafy, 5=ultra dense) (5)

items.grow_notes:
Hey,



I bought 3 seeds and grew them indoors, 1 didn't sprout, journal in the signature...



This was my first time growing and I must say I'm very pleased with the results.



I'd say it was a good wield, about 60 grams / 2.11644 ounces from 2 plants, for the lights I had I think it's ok, next time I'll improve things.



Very pungent smell, very strong smell, very hard to contain when transporting, I had to use several baggies.



Dense buds, easy to trim.



Mostly a body high that makes me wanna sit or lay down, makes me sleep like a rock, I feel better rested in the morning with the same hours of sleep.



There's also a mental high and some euphoria, I like to play video games while under but my performance drops considerably, I start to wonder in my thoughts and imagination while I leave my character on auto pilot...



After 1 month of curing the smell is just great, I find myself smelling a bud long after rolling my joint. I also like the taste when I'm about to light her up and during the first hits.



Duration is average for me.



Potency is strong for me.



Overall a classic that lives up to the name, all my friends wanted to get some of it,

items.excerpt:
There are a couple of classic strains in the global world of extra potent marijuana that have been around for a very long time, fascinating both growers and smokers with their superb qualities, having reached a legendary status. Ak-47 for sure is one of these outstanding evergreens, besides e.g. Skunk#1, Northern Lights, Haze or White Widow. For Simon, master breeder of Serious Seeds, finding the unique AK-47 genetic profile was the rare case of a ?lucky punch? every cannabis seed breeder dreams of. In 1992, after having tested thousands of experimental plants of different breeding lines, he finally achieved his goal of creating a high-quality sativa/indica strain with excellent overall properties and a lot of charisma - the AK-47 was born. Although Simon keeps the exact pedigree of AK-47 as a secret, like the composition of Coca Cola, he reveals that it was bred from Colombian, Mexican, Thai and Afghani seed stock, resulting in a 50:50 indica/sativa hybrid.

After having finished a new strain and releasing it to the market, Simon uses to keep on working on the genetic formula and partly rebuilds the strains after some years by using previously unused material within the same genetic line as new parent, thus refreshing genetics. The trade-mark characteristics of the strain are basically maintained thereby, only the accents are shifted a little bit. This practice is the reason why Simon`s small, but exclusive seed collection never loses its fascination and dynamics. Imagine for example that during your breeding proces you choose from each generation the shortest, fattest, mostly kick-ass plants for next parents all the time. Indeed, the % stays the same whatever plants you choose, but the plants effect and looks will be more what we call indica like. Such is the case more or less.

On the whole, AK-47 has won 8 prizes, covering a time period of one decade! Forever young could really be the motto of AK-47.

With its currently predominating indica characteristics, AK-47 tends to grow to a medium-sized plant with only moderate side-branching, making for a large fat main cola along with several excellent secondary tops. Hence the overall yield can be way above average, Serious Seeds declares 350-500 g per m2 as achievable under good indoor conditions, after 53-63 days of flowering - which is a pretty good time deal, regarding the AK`s outstanding qualities in both high and aroma. AK leafs are dark-green, showing more of the indica spectrum, but not as wide as full indica leafs. What is remarkable is the fact that also after the latest indica approach in the AK breeding process, Simon managed to maintain that sativa-tpyical high calyx-to-leaf ratio which means lots of flowers and only a few leafs. The single AK calyx size tends to be unsually large, resulting in fat clusters grouping together very decoratively and densely, contributing to the trade-mark appearance of AK-47. These fluffy, compact nuggs ooze lots of glistening trichomes and break up nicely, leaving plenty of resinous crystals on your fingers, unleashing an unusually strong, sweet and fruity aroma.

The AK`s name shall by no means be understood as being aggressively intended or following any military tradition, but rather express the special effect that sets in when one smokes the AK, sometimes proving as a real one hit wonder, made possible by a THC content of 20% (measured by an independent laboratory). Apart from that, the high is also very complex, clearly pronouncing elements of both sides of the cannabis spectrum. But as the indica aspect is presently predominating the AK, first of all it quickly provides a heavy, long-lasting stonedness. However, there`s still also enough sativa power to parallely effect a cerebral up-high that prevents the smoker from ?getting totally hypnotized? or even falling asleep. The taste is spicy-sweet, not harsh at all, sometimes with a slight sandalwood undertone ? on the whole, satisfying any connoisseurs' taste.

items.name_norm: skunky skunk
items.thread_title: "Skunky" Skunk
items.grow_notes:
Strain Name: “Skunky” Skunk

From: Trinity Gardens Collective

When: May 2010

Grade: A-

Type: Hybrid of several skunk phenos

Price: $150/half oz.

Looks: Light green with orange hairs - with a nice crystal coating

Smell: Fresh greens with a slight citrus smell

Taste: Not too strong in flavor, the smoke was fairly expansive and caught me off-guard...had me hacking/coughing.

Buzz Type: The buzz hit really hard due to the “over-toke” on my first bong hit. A few more tokes, and I was enjoying a nice cerebral buzz, that was just short of being trippy/spacey. The buzz was staged, in that the body high crept up after about 30 minutes of a mostly cerebral buzz.

Buzz Length: Medium-Long – the buzz lasted for around 1.5-2 hours.

Best Medicinal Use: Overall mind and body relaxation.

Overall: Similar to other skunk strains I’ve had, smoked most of the day, with little crash. A good mix of head and body buzz, with a nondescript taste/smell. Reminds me of the “old days” when there weren’t so many boutique strains around, and good bud was either green or reddish/gold.

Nirvana Soul Diesel review

Sour Diesel is basically a New York Power Diesel back-crossed with one of its ancestors - the mouth-watering Sour Diesel. Yield indoor High (450-600gr/M2)

Plant height Tall (More Than 200cm)

Photoperiod flowering time 9 To 11 Weeks

Northern hemisphere harvest October

Suitable climates - Dry

Aroma - Earthy

Sour Diesel Feminized is a sativa dominant, tall lady that is more demanding and a little harder to grow than most strains. A vigorous, large yielding hybrid that reeks of petroleum, lemons with a powerful pungent citrus edge. She offers a giggly, dreamy and blissful effect that is perfect for social scenarios as well as daytime use.

Genetics: By crossing two of the most aromatic Cannabis strains around, we were able to create a moderately difficult to grow hybrid, that enhances the best from Chem Dog and Super Skunk. Expect an exceptional resin profile and large, stacked buds that will ripen with dark purple hues.

Strain Characteristics: Best suited for growers with a few indoors grows under their belt, this fast growing, high maintenance sativa dominant hybrid, will grow tall with long side branches. She is an excellent candidate for plant training such as tying down, topping and pruning, where she can reward you with harvests of 400- 500 g/m² making her a big producer.

Her THC levels will range from 16-20%, and flowering time will range from 9-11 weeks. Once flowering begins, the plants will stretch considerably in height, so growers with limited space should be careful, or apply plant training prior to the changing the timers to 12/12. She will really bulk up during the final 3 weeks of blooming, and be encrusted in trichomes. Sour Diesel Feminized will begin to change color during the final few weeks, where she will reveal various shades of purple, red and magenta.

Experiencing this strain: The effects of Sour Diesel Feminized can be described as an exuberant mental boost, that becomes both happy, giggly and an overall sense of taking it easy. A very social strain that can have you deep in conversation jumping from one topic to another with reckless abandon. She is incredible for creative individuals, musicians, writers, artists, deep reading, gaming and long walks in nature, or a day at the beach.

There is my list which I need to sort out:

 The most probable candidates: 

Blueberry - Dutch Passion - 80% Indica, 20% Sativa

AK 47 - Serio

items.grow_notes:
Strawberry Frog – Small Potatoes Seeds Strain Review

Strawberry Kush x Vader OG

This review is going to be a little different, with the description of the crossed strains.

Will up date this after 6 to 8 weeks of curing.

 Strawberry Kush is sweet, strong and truly well-rounded. This strain certainly justifies its lineage and contains a musky artificial strawberry taste with a THC content of up to 23 percent. It is essentially found as a cross between the bitter OG Kush and the sugary Strawberry Cough and is mostly strong but not overwhelming.

This strain typically blossoms in eight to nine weeks and is obtainable by cloning only. In its make-up, Strawberry Kush contains Sativa genetics and it is smoked more as a Sativa than an Indica.

items.name_norm: super lemon haze
items.thread_title: Super Lemon Haze
items.grow_notes:
Super Lemon Haze, from Nameless Genetics

I bought an eighth of Super Lemon Haze from the dispo in February with the intention of conducting a bit of citizen science with it. 

It was the freshest batch available that day, and got the brief for another idea I had (when life gives you lemons, smoke lemon haze).

I wanted to photograph trichomes over time to see what effect she will have on them, so I needed to create a replicable setup to take pictures of the same area reach time. 

I taped paper to a cutting board, traced the outline of the base of an extra hands device, and set all of that in my photo box up against the edge in the corner. I clipped a piece of bud into the device and shot the first set of images. 

When it's not being photographed, it lives under a large Ocktoberfest mug to keep the dust off. 

I photograph it twice a month, and vape a little of the remaining flower each time. 

It has a very citrus forward flavor and smokes well, as one expects from a premium brand like Nameless. 

The effects are pleasant and uplifting, personally. Individual results may vary

Sweet Seeds Flashback #2

I grew this in FF Happy Frog using @geoflora nutrient line. The @GeoFlora Nutrients made this a very easy straight forward grow with no real issues to speak of. Light source was a @ViparSpectra XS-2000. I did not scrog her and got about 6 oz.'s of final dry product. The buds have a fairly firm structure and on average about the size of a quarter. With a pleasant aroma of Strawberries. I did not play very much during this grow mainly, because it has been a few years, since I did a soil grow. So needless to say, my harvest was small, but enough to enjoy. I am thinking about doing soil grows during the summer months when heat is a factor.

The Geoflora nutrient line made growing in soil a breeze. Just follow their feed schedule and you can’t go wrong. I when and bought a 2-gallon sprayer so when I top dress her, I get better saturation of the nutrients deeper into the soil. I would highly recommend use this line of nutrients, especially if you are new to growing, or looking for a better nutrient line.

Welcome to the Late Start flower journal. I thought I wanted to stop journaling but found myself looking for other places to post. Growing is good for me it gives me something rewarding to focus on. Growing are four strains in soil. All are from @Barney's Farm . They are being grown in a 4’ x 4’. There is the Sour Diesel, OG Kush, Girl Scout Cookies and Strawberry Lemonade. They are growing under a 600w, F.O.G, Air Grow Pro III, using @Remo Nutrients 

There are 11 plants total. 9 plants in 11 liter pots, 1 in a 6 liter, and a last in a 1.75 liter. All hard pots. The plants were vegged for 25 days. Today is grow day 49, and day 24 of 12/12. A couple plants were supercropped a few days ago as they were getting too tall. The upper canopy is now at approximately 105cm with some plants still stretching a little.

Attached are some pictures from this week. The GSC fan leaves have the red leaf stems.

Thanks for looking in. Happy grows

items.grow_notes: Hey 420. Today's strain review will be of Heavy Grapefruit from Europa Seeds. This plant is a cross between Sweet Tooth and Dynamite and is mostly indica. She is vigorous in veg growing fast and bushy with some good side branching. When you put her into flower she slows down a bit and has a relatively short stretch over the first few weeks. One thing that ironically stood out was that she was quite unassuming and didn't catch my eye as several other strains did throughout the flowering period. She is advertised as an 8 week strain however this one went to 10 before I harvested her so not as fast as most indicas I've grown over the last year. She hermied like crazy and was producing literally bunches of bananas right at the end so I pulled her from the tent. It wasn't a problem though as she had reached full maturity and was ready for harvesting. She was also a very easy plant to grow. Her buds were very dense and heavy for their size. She has a very pungent and sharp tropical fruit smell that reminds me of the summer when I break open a bud. It is a bit sour but mainly sweet with grape tones coming through. Her taste is better than she smells as it has a candy flavour that's hidden

She has a very pungent and sharp tropical fruit smell that reminds me of the summer when I break open a bud. It is a bit sour but mainly sweet with grape tones coming through. Her taste is better than she smells as it has a candy flavour that's hidden from the nose. It's a taste that reminds me of my childhood when I used to eat a lot of sweets that had strong artificial flavours. It's very fruity and has just a little hint of hash to finish it off. It really is a great taste. The effects for this one are fairly one sided with it being right down the sleepy, pain relieving end. She's a great relaxant and is mind numbing if you have that bit to much. She helped me to forget that I had a headache and allowed me to fall asleep not long after having only a small joint. This one made me look blazed though with fire red eyes peeping through narrow slits making my vision a bit lazy to say the least. Dry mouth and thirst is also something you'll likely encounter but it's so worth it for it's satisfying deep smoke. So overall I'm very impressed. Even though she hermied at the end and took a little longer than most she gave us some great, high quality smoke that has good bag appeal, great flavours and a knockout punch in return. Her yields were also great for her size making her good for growers who need to work in small spaces. Not too bad at all....

items.thread_title: The Top Strain of the 1980's
items.grow_notes:
1980 - 1989

 Most Popular Strain of the 1980s 

Though strains like Northern Lights, Afghani #1, and Haze received significant attention, Skunk #1 stands out as the era’s most purchased and consumed cannabis variety. Developed in California by Sacred Seeds (notably by “Sam the Skunkman”) and refined in the Netherlands, Skunk #1 combined Afghani (Indica) with Colombian and Mexican (Sativa) genetics. Its potent, stable hybrid profile and short flowering time made it a favorite among both indoor and outdoor growers, ultimately shaping much of the commercial cannabis seed market during the decade.

 Context 

 BREEDING LEGACY 

 - Skunk #1’s genetics served as the backbone for countless future hybrids (e.g., Cheese, Shiva Skunk, and Super Skunk). 

 - Its trademark skunky aroma was a hallmark of the strain’s distinct terpene profile and often drew consumers seeking both potency and a notable scent.

 POPULARITY INDICATIONS 
​

"What about the Smoke Report...?" 

When trimming I always make mistakes and I ended up with some smokeable 'PAWTS!' I threw those into the fridge for a few days and then on top of a tent to finish drying up. She smoked nice for not being cured & was tastey from the bong. I shredded some up for my dry herbal vape, The Kind Pen by TruVa', and man... those terps are super good. Some nice light flavors mixed with a hint of black licorice! Really Tastey! And, I don't even like Black Licorice... I smoked a bowl and went for a bike ride round the neighborhood. Great high, I could think but I was super high, by far the best weed I've smoked to date! Great High! 

Start and grow this strain in at least a 5 gallon container, give her 18/6 lighting from the word go, light feedings (find an auto feeding schedule before you start), and keep an eye on those trichs the last 3 weeks, especially if you're running this strain in cooler temps. Only one thing left for you to do. 

GET AND GROW THIS STRAIN!!!!!

items.grow_notes:
Strain Name - White Widow

 Seed Bank - Crop King Seeds

 When - 07/19

 Price - Free/$100

 Type - 60% Indica, 40% Sativa

 Appearance - Light green, long orange and white hairs. Not very dense (Probably didn't flower long enough).

 Smell - Skunky

 Taste - Smooth and clean

 Type of Buzz - Heavy body stone. Very couch lock.

 Length of Buzz - around 2 hours. I'm a heavy user. THC content can get up to 24%.

 Best Medicinal Use - Insomnia, appetite enhancement, pain relief, anti-anxiety

 Overall - White widow remains one of my top 10 strains. The smell was very skunky yet almost with a hint of fruity. The leaves were covered in trichomes. The nugs were slightly fluffy. The smoke was very smooth. The taste was "clean", as in it it did not taste bad, but was not full of flavor. Overall I'd rate the smoke 8 out of 10. The high itself is immediate. It hits you pretty hard all over your body and head. It's a major couch lock high.

items.name: White Widow Feminized Royal Queen Seeds (RQS)
items.name_norm: white widow feminized royal queen seeds rqs
items.thread_title: White Widow Feminized Royal Queen Seeds (RQS)
items.grow_notes:
Hey folks, names Chad from Ohio. This like my third fourth run, but first feminized alone. Im feeding Foop nutes n sugar supplement as well. Right now she's under 320 watt full spectrum led, five gal. pot. Mix is actually from Menards. It's a neutral soil with mycorrhizae. It's very nice actually. I'd get it again. I use r/o water n pH usually like 6.0-6.2. Humidity is like 60% n temps r high right now 80° because it's hot. But I got good air flow over them so canopy shouldn't bake tbh. I just dropped lights like 8" to increase lux from 16, 500 to like 25,000 because I'm still vegging. I just tucked the head down again because I wanted more light to reach that area because I noticed some veg I'd like to pull up. U see I'm shootn for flat canopy n big nug. I'm thinking she's like three weeks old possibly four. I'm looking to determine time to start flowering tbh. Any thoughts question is appreciated. Thank you. Good day folks. 

Btw, the dust is sevendust. Had to eliminate infestation of aphids from recent harvest brought in from outside. Aphids gone. I'll just wash nugs with bud wash solution I learned already from some brothers on here.

items.name: Zora21's Cookies Gelato & OG Kush Grow Journal Ft. Mars TS3000
items.name_norm: zora21 s cookies gelato og kush grow journal ft mars ts3000
items.thread_title: Zora21's Cookies Gelato & OG Kush Grow Journal Ft. Mars TS3000
items.grow_notes:
Hi, welcome to my journal. I believe last time I tried this was in 2017 and it didn't go well. This time I'm very much dedicated to journaling at least for my own documentation and learning.

1st seed(OG Kush freebie) started germinating roughly march 14 and took about 7 days to germinate because it got incredibly cold because my house furnace failed. Luckily I warmed it up and it continued.

2nd seed(Cookies Gelato) started germinating, just cracked the shell and then stopped germinating so I trashed it. This will be the last time mentioning this one.

3rd seed(Cookies Gelato) started germinating April 3rd and popped from its pot yesterday April 7th.

4th seed(Cookies Gelato) started in pot April 6th as I wasn't sure the 3rd was going to pop but here we are. Yet to sprout to surface.

OG Kush is sitting roughly 17 days veg, it's been an weird mutated plant since the beginning (leaf twisting/growing partial leafs). I was traveling so it got an early up pot which slowed growth. It's finally setting into it's new home and showing signs of magnesium deficiency I think?

 Strain/s : Cookies Gelato & OG Kush

 Genetic Makeup : Hybrid Sativa

 Pot/Bucket Size : 15gal fabric pot vivosun
